What Anas ibn al-Nadr found may belong to either category, and Allah knows best.

Abu Nu'aym said: Muhammad ibn Ma'mar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mu'adhdhin narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, al-Rabi' ibn Badr informed us, Harun ibn Riyab narrated to us, from Mujahid, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The fragrance of Paradise is perceived from a distance of five hundred years."

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Tarif narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, Jabir al-Ju'fi related to me, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The fragrance of Paradise is perceived from a distance of a thousand years, and by Allah, an undutiful son and one who severs the ties of kinship will not smell it."

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever claims to be the son of someone other than his father will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance is perceived from a distance of five hundred years. Allah, glorified is He, has indeed shown His servants in this abode some traces of Paradise and a sample of it: its pleasant fragrance, its desirable delights, its beautiful sights, its good fruits, its bliss, its joy, and the coolness of the eye."

**[Section: On the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq)]**

It took place in the fifth year after the Hijrah, in Shawwal, according to the more correct of the two opinions, since there is no dispute that the Battle of Uhud was in Shawwal of the third year. The polytheists had promised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a meeting in the following year, which was the fourth year, but then they broke their promise because of the drought of that year, and they returned. When the fifth year came, they came to fight him. This is the view of the people of the biographies and the military campaigns (Ahl al-Siyar wa al-Maghazi).

Musa ibn Uqbah differed with them and said: "Rather, it was in the fourth year." Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm said: "This is the correct view about which there is no doubt." He argued for it with the hadith of Ibn Umar in the Sahihayn, that he was presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud when he was fourteen years old, and he was not permitted [to fight]; then he was presented to him on the day of the Trench when he was fifteen years old, and he was permitted.

He said: "So it is established that there was only one year between them."

This was answered with two replies. The first: Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him back because he considered him too young for fighting, and permitted him when he reached the age at which he was seen to be capable. There is nothing in this that denies that the interval between them could have been a year or so.

The second: Perhaps the Battle of Uhud was at the beginning of his fourteenth year, and the Battle of the Trench at the end of his fifteenth year.

**[The cause of the Battle of the Trench]**

The cause of the Battle of the Trench was that when the Jews saw the victory of the polytheists over the Muslims at Uhud, and when they learned of Abu Sufyan's appointment to attack the Muslims, he went out for that purpose. Then he returned in the following year. The leaders of the Jews, such as Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Sallam ibn Mishkam, Kinanah ibn al-Rabi' and others, went out to the Quraysh in Makkah to incite them to attack the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and to stir them up against him, and they promised them on their own behalf to support them. The Quraysh responded to them. Then they went out to Ghatafan and called them, and they responded to them. Then they went around among the Arab tribes calling them to this, and whoever responded, responded. So the Quraysh went out, led by Abu Sufyan, with four thousand men. The Banu Sulaym joined them at Marr al-Zahran. The Banu Asad, Fazarah, Ashja' and Banu Murrah went out, and Ghatafan came with their leader Uyaynah ibn Hisn. The number of disbelievers who reached the Trench was ten thousand.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of their march against him, he consulted the Companions. Salman al-Farisi advised him to dig a trench which would stand between the enemy and Madinah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered it, and the Muslims hastened to it, and he himself worked in it. They also hastened to pre-empt the assault of the disbelievers against them. In the digging of the trench there were signs of his prophethood and marks of his messengership, of which the reports are widely transmitted. The digging of the Trench was in front of Sal', and Sal' is a mountain behind the backs of the Muslims, while the Trench lay between them and the disbelievers.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with three thousand Muslims. He was protected by the mountain at his back, and by the Trench in front of them.

Ibn Ishaq said: "He went out with seven hundred," but this is an error, derived from [the number who went out] at Uhud.

The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered the women and children to be placed in the fortified towers of Madinah, and he appointed Ibn Umm Maktum as their deputy.

Huyayy ibn Akhtab set out to the Banu Qurayzah and approached their fortress. Ka'b ibn Asad refused to open it for him, but he kept speaking to him until he opened it for him. When he entered upon him, he said: "I have come to you with the honour of the age. I have come to you with the Quraysh, Ghatafan and Asad, under their commanders, to fight Muhammad." Ka'b said: "By Allah, you have come to me with the humiliation of the age, and with a cloud whose water has been poured out; it thunders and flashes, but there is nothing in it."

He kept at him until he broke the covenant between himself and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and joined the polytheists in fighting him. The polytheists rejoiced at this. Ka'b stipulated with Huyayy that if they did not overcome Muhammad, he would come and enter his fortress with him, and suffer what he suffered. Huyayy agreed to this and fulfilled it to him.

News of the Banu Qurayzah and their breaking of the covenant reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he sent to them al-Sa'dayn (Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn Ubadah), Khawwat ibn Jubayr, and Abdullah ibn Rawahah, to find out whether they were still upholding their covenant or had broken it. When they drew near to them, they found them in the worst condition: they openly reviled them with abuse and hostility, and they insulted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So they withdrew from them and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) using indirect words to inform him that they had broken the covenant and acted treacherously. This was grievous to the Muslims. At that, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Allahu Akbar! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!"

The trial intensified, hypocrisy appeared, and some of the Banu Harithah asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to go back to Madinah, saying: ﴿Indeed our houses are exposed, though they were not exposed. They only intended to flee.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13].

The Banu Salamah were inclined to cowardice, but then Allah made both groups firm.

The polytheists remained besieging the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a month, and there was no fighting between them, because of what Allah had placed of the Trench between them and the Muslims, except that some horsemen of the Quraysh, among them Amr ibn Abd Wudd and a group with him, came towards the Trench. When they stood at it, they said: "This is a stratagem which the Arabs did not know." Then they aimed for a narrow place in the Trench, forced their way across it, and their horses roamed in the salt flat between the Trench and Sal'. They called for single combat, and Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) volunteered for Amr. He fought him, and Allah killed him at his hands. He had been one of the bravest and champions of the polytheists. The rest fled back to their companions. (The war-cry of the Muslims that day was: "Ha Mim, they will not be helped.")

When this situation had lasted long for the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to make peace with Uyaynah ibn Hisn and al-Harith ibn Awf, the two chiefs of Ghatafan, on one third of the produce of Madinah, in return for them withdrawing with their people. Negotiations on this took place. He consulted the two Sa'ds about this. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, if Allah has commanded you this, then we hear and obey. But if it is something you are doing for our sake, we have no need of it. We and these people were upon polytheism and the worship of idols, and they did not expect to eat any of its fruit except as hospitality or by purchase. Now that Allah has honoured us with Islam and guided us to it, and strengthened us through you, shall we give them our wealth? By Allah, we will give them nothing but the sword." So he approved their opinion and said: "This was only something I was doing for you, because I saw the Arabs had shot at you with a single bow."

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to Him belongs all praise, brought about a matter from His side by which He defeated the enemy, routed their hosts, and broke their strength. Among the means He prepared for this was that a man from Ghatafan, named Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud ibn Amir (may Allah be pleased with him), came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have embraced Islam, so command me as you wish." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are only one man, so cause discord among them on our behalf as far as you are able, for war is deception." He went at once to the Banu Qurayza, who had been his allies in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam). He entered upon them while they did not know of his conversion, and said: "O Banu Qurayza, you have fought Muhammad, and Quraysh, if they find an opportunity, will seize it; otherwise they will turn back to their own lands and leave you alone with Muhammad, who will then take his revenge on you." They said: "So what is to be done, O Nu'aym?" He said: "Do not fight alongside them until they give you hostages." They said: "You have given sound advice." Then he went on his way to Quraysh and said to them: "You know my affection for you and my sincere counsel to you." They said: "Yes." He said: "The Jews have regretted what they did in breaking their covenant with Muhammad and his companions, and they have sent word to him that they will take hostages from you and hand them over to him, and then they will side with him against you. So if they ask you for hostages, do not give them any." Then he went to Ghatafan and said to them the same thing.

When it was the night of Saturday in Shawwal, they sent to the Jews: "We are not a people who can remain in one place. The horses and the camels have perished, so rise up with us so that we may engage Muhammad." The Jews sent back to them: "Tomorrow is Saturday, and you know what befell those before us when they transgressed on it. Besides, we will not fight alongside you until you send us hostages."

When their messengers returned with this reply, Quraysh said: "Nu'aym has told you the truth, by Allah." They sent to the Jews: "By Allah, we will not send anyone to you. So come out with us until we engage Muhammad." Qurayza said: "Nu'aym has told you the truth, by Allah." Thus the two parties fell apart, and Allah sent against the polytheists a host of wind, which overturned their tents and left them no cooking pot without spilling it and no tent peg without uprooting it, so that they had no place of rest. And the host of Allah from the angels shook them and cast terror and fear into their hearts.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman to bring him news of them. He found them in this condition, already preparing to depart. He returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him of the departure of the people. In the morning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) found that Allah had turned back His enemy in their rage, having gained no good, and that Allah had spared him the fighting. He fulfilled His promise, strengthened His host, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone. The Messenger (ﷺ) entered Medina and laid down his weapons. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him while he was bathing in the house of Umm Salama and said: "Have you laid down your weapons? The angels have not yet laid down their weapons. Rise up to the expedition against these people," meaning the Banu Qurayza. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out:
"Whoever is listening and obeying, let him not pray the afternoon prayer except in the land of Banu Qurayza."
The Muslims set out swiftly. What happened to him and to the Banu Qurayza was as we have already mentioned. On the Day of the Trench and the Day of Qurayza, about ten of the Muslims were martyred.

[Section: The assassination of Abu Rafi' by Abdullah ibn Unays]

We have already mentioned that Abu Rafi' was among those who incited the confederates against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was not killed along with the Banu Qurayza, as his companion Huyayy ibn Akhtab was killed. The Khazraj desired to kill him, to match the Aws in killing Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. Allah, glorified and exalted, had made these two tribes vie with one another before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in good deeds. So they asked him for permission to kill him, and he granted it. Men from the Banu Salama were appointed for this, all of them from that clan: Abdullah ibn Atik, who was the leader of the group; Abdullah ibn Unays; Abu Qatada al-Harith ibn Rib'i; Mas'ud ibn Sinan; and Khuzaa'i ibn al-Aswad. They traveled until they reached him at Khaybar, in his house. They descended upon him at night, killed him, and returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Each of them claimed to have killed him. He said: "Show me your swords." When they showed him, he said of the sword of Abdullah ibn Unays: "This is the one that killed him; I see in it traces of food."

**The Ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ Regarding the Choice Given to His Wives Between Remaining with Him and Separating from Him**

It is established in the *Sahihayn* (the two *Sahih* collections) from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to give his wives the choice, he began with me and said: 'I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm in your not hurrying until you consult your parents.' She said: 'He knew that my parents would not have ordered me to leave him.' Then he recited: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release. And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾"

She said: "So I said, 'About this, should I consult my parents? For I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode.' ʿĀʾishah said: 'Then the wives of the Prophet ﷺ did the same as I did, and that was not a divorce (*ṭalāq*).'"

Rabiʿah and Ibn Shihab said: "One of them chose herself, so she left, and it was an irrevocable divorce (*al-battah*)." Ibn Shihab said: "She was a Bedouin woman." ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb said: "She was the daughter of al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-ʿĀmiriyyah, and she returned to her family." Ibn Ḥabīb said: "He had consummated the marriage with her." End of quotation.

It has also been said that he had not consummated the marriage with her, and that she afterwards used to gather dung, saying: "I am the unfortunate one."

People differed concerning this choice in two respects:

The first: what was the choice about?

The second: what is its ruling?

As for the first, the view held by the majority (*al-jumhūr*) is that it was a choice between remaining with him and separation. ʿAbd al-Razzāq, in his *Muṣannaf*, reported from al-Ḥasan that Allah, exalted is He, only gave them the choice between this world and the Hereafter, and did not give them the choice regarding divorce. But the context of the Qur'an and the saying of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, refute his statement. There is no doubt that He, glorified is He, gave them the choice between Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, on the one hand, and the life of this world and its adornment, on the other. He made the consequence of their choosing Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode to be remaining with His Messenger, and the consequence of their choosing the worldly life and its adornment to be that He would provide for them and release them with a fair release, which is divorce, without any doubt or dispute.

[The choice was between remaining with him and separation]

As for their disagreement about its ruling, it concerns two points:

The first: the ruling when the wife chooses her husband.

The second: the ruling when she chooses herself.

As for the first, the view held by the majority of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, all of his wives, and the majority of the Muslim community is that the woman who chose her husband is not divorced, and that the choice by itself is not a divorce. This was reported from ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and ʿĀʾishah. (ʿĀʾishah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us the choice, so we chose him," and we did not count it as a divorce. It was also reported from Umm Salamah, Qarībah, her sister, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr.)

It is authentically reported from ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thābit, and a group of the Companions that if she chose her husband, it is a single revocable divorce (*ṭalqah rajʿiyyah*). This is the view of al-Ḥasan, and it is a narration from Aḥmad, reported from him by Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr, who said: "If she chose her husband, it is one divorce in which he retains the right of return (*raj'ah*); and if she chose herself, it is three divorces." Abū Bakr said: "Isḥāq ibn Manṣūr alone reported this, and the practice is according to what the majority narrated."

The author of *al-Mughnī* said: "The basis of this narration is that the choice is an allusive expression (*kināyah*) by which the husband intended divorce, so it takes effect by the mere utterance, like his other allusive expressions. This is what ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, explicitly stated, and the truth is with her in rejecting and refuting this view. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was chosen by his wives, he did not say that a divorce had taken effect upon them, nor did he take them back. She is the most knowledgeable of the Muslim community regarding the matter of the choice. It is authentically reported from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: 'That was not a divorce.' In another wording: 'We did not count it as a divorce.' In another wording: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave us the choice; was that a divorce?'"

What led those who said it is a revocable divorce to this view is that the choice is a grant of ownership (*tamlīk*), and a woman cannot own herself except after she has been divorced. Therefore the grant of ownership necessarily entails the occurrence of divorce. This view rests on two premises: first, that the choice is a grant of ownership; and second, that a grant of ownership necessarily entails the occurrence of divorce. Both premises are disputed. The choice is not a grant of ownership. Even if it were a grant of ownership, it would not necessarily entail the occurrence of divorce before the one who was granted it exercised it. The most that can be said is that the wife comes to own it, just as the husband used to own it, and so it does not take effect without the one who owns it exercising it. Even if what they mentioned were correct, it would make the divorce irrevocable (*bā'in*), because a woman who is in a revocable divorce does not own herself.

**[Section: The strength of faith and knowledge, whose possessor is forgiven what others are not forgiven]**

If it is said: You have mentioned that the one who loves is forgiven what others are not forgiven, and that the close friend is pardoned what is not pardoned to others. Likewise the scholar too: he is forgiven what is not forgiven to the ignorant person, as al-Tabarani narrated with a good chain (isnad), traced back (marfu') to the Prophet (ﷺ): "When Allah, glorified is He, gathers the people on the Day of Resurrection in one plain, He will say to the scholars: 'I was worshipped by your fatwas (legal opinions). I know that you used to mix [truth and falsehood] as people mix. I did not place My knowledge in you while intending to punish you. Go, for I have forgiven you.'" This is the meaning of the hadith, and it has been reported both connected (musnad) and with a broken chain (mursal).

What you have mentioned is correct, and it is the requirement of wisdom, generosity and benevolence. But what will you do with the doubled punishment that was threatened concerning those [close ones] should something disliked occur from them? Such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little. Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] of life and double [punishment] of death; then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us﴾ [al-Isra': 74-75]. That is: had We not made you firm, you would have nearly inclined toward them to some degree; and had you done so, We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, meaning We would have doubled the punishment for you in this world and the Hereafter.

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some sayings [of his own invention], We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44-46]. That is: if he had brought something from himself, We would have seized him by his right hand, cut the cords of his heart, and destroyed him. Allah protected him from inclining toward his enemies by the smallest particle of his heart, and from attributing [falsehood] to Him, glorified is He. How many there are who incline toward His enemies and attribute [things] to Him from their own selves, yet He has given them respite and has not regarded them, like all the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah), who attribute [falsehoods] to His names, attributes and religion.

What you mentioned in the story of Yunus (Jonah) belongs to this category, for he was not forgiven for one display of anger, and he was imprisoned for it in the belly of the fish. And the condition of the father of mankind suffices, where he was not pardoned for one morsel, and it was the cause of his expulsion from Paradise.

The answer is that this too is true, and there is no contradiction between the two matters. Whoever has had Allah's blessing perfected upon him, and been singled out from it with what others were not singled out with, in that He gave him what He denied others, is favored with bounty, honored with generosity, given greater nearness, and placed in the station of the beloved friend. His state requires preserving the rank of closeness, nearness and special favor, so that he must guard his station from the slightest disturbance or severance. Because of the intensity of care for him, his greater closeness, his being taken as one's own, and his being chosen above others, the rights of his Master and Lord over him are more complete, His blessings upon him more perfect, and what is required of him is greater than what is required of others. So if he becomes heedless and falls short of what his rank demands, he is alerted with what the distant outsider is not alerted with, while he is still forgiven what that outsider is not forgiven. Thus both matters come together in his case.

If you wish to know how the two come together without contradiction, reality bears witness to it: the king pardons his special servants and friends what he does not pardon one who is not in their rank, and he takes them to account and disciplines them with what he does not apply to others. We have mentioned evidences for this and that, and there is no contradiction between the two matters.

And if you have two slaves, or two sons, or two wives, one of whom is more beloved to you, closer to your heart, and dearer to you, you treat him with both of these matters, and the two treatments come together in his case according to his nearness to you, your love for him, and his dearness to you. When you consider the perfection of your kindness to him and the completion of your blessing upon him, his treatment requires [stricter] dealings with him, with what you do not apply to anyone else, such as admonition and not neglecting him. And when you consider his kindness and love toward you, his obedience and service, the perfection of his servitude, sincerity and counsel, you forgive him and pardon him, with what you do not do with others. Thus the two treatments are according to what comes from you and what comes from him.

This meaning has also been shown to be considered in the Shari'ah, where the punishment for one who has been blessed with marriage and then commits fornication is stoning (rajm), while the punishment for one who has not been given this blessing is flogging (jald). Likewise, the punishment is doubled for the free person who has been given ownership of himself, whose blessing has been perfected, and who has not been made the property of another; and the punishment for the slave, who is deficient by reason of slavery and has not received this blessing, is half of that.

Glory be to Him whose wisdom in His creation, command and recompense has dazzled the minds of all worlds, and whose wisdom testifies that He is the Most Wise of the wise.

﻿The poet said:
*For Allah there is a secret beneath every subtle thing,*
*and the one of insight dives deep, seeking it.*

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 33, verse 32:**

He commanded them not to be soft in their speech, as a woman who is inclined to give in is soft in her manner of speaking, so that the one in whose heart is a disease of desire would be tempted. Yet they should not be so harsh in speech that it approaches indecency, but should "speak in a good manner."

**(Fa'ida, a benefit or point of note)**

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women, if you are mindful of God. So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should be tempted, but speak a fair word.﴾

When He commanded them to have taqwa (God-consciousness), which by its nature entails humility and gentleness of speech, He forbade them from being soft in speech, lest the one with a disease in his heart should set his hopes on them. Then He commanded them to speak "a fair word," to remove any notion that permission had been granted to speak what is reprehensible, since they had been forbidden to be soft in speech.

**(Fasl, a section)**

God, glory be to Him, created the son of Adam and his limbs, and He made for each limb a perfection, such that when it lacks it, it feels pain. He also made a perfection for its ruler, which is the heart, such that when it lacks that perfection, its illnesses and pains arrive at it: anxieties, griefs and sorrows.

When the eye lacks what it was created for, which is the power of sight, and the ear lacks what it was created for, which is the power of hearing, and the tongue lacks what it was created for, which is the power of speech, each loses its perfection.

As for the heart, it was created to know its Originator, to love Him, to affirm His oneness, to rejoice in Him, to delight in His love, to be pleased with Him, to rely upon Him, to love for His sake, to hate for His sake, to be loyal for His sake, to be hostile for His sake, to remember Him continually, and for Him to be dearer to it than all else, more hopeful of Him than of all else, and greater in its heart than all else. It has no bliss, no joy, no pleasure, and indeed no life except through this. This is for the heart like nourishment, health and life. When it lacks its nourishment, its health and its life, then anxieties, griefs and sorrows rush at it from every direction and settle upon it.

Among the greatest of its diseases are: shirk (association of partners with God), sins, heedlessness, making light of what He loves and what pleases Him, abandoning entrusting affairs to Him, weak reliance upon Him, inclining toward other than Him, discontent with what He decrees, and doubt concerning His promise and His threat.

When you reflect on the diseases of the heart, you will find that these matters and their like are its causes, with no other cause for them. Its cure, for which there is no other cure, is what these prophetic remedies contain of matters opposed to these diseases. For a disease is removed by its opposite, and health is preserved by its like. Thus its health is preserved by these prophetic matters, and its diseases are cured by their opposites.

So tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) opens for the servant the door of goodness, joy, pleasure, happiness and delight. Repentance is the purging of the humours and corrupt matter that are the cause of its ailments, and a protective regimen against overindulgence. It closes off from him the doors of evil, so the door of felicity and goodness is opened for him through tawhid, and the door of evil is closed through repentance and seeking forgiveness.

Some of the earlier leaders of medicine said: "Whoever wants the health of the body, let him reduce food and drink; and whoever wants the health of the heart, let him abandon sins."

Thabit ibn Qurrah said: "The rest of the body lies in eating less, the rest of the spirit lies in committing fewer sins, and the rest of the tongue lies in speaking less."

Sins are to the heart like poisons: if they do not destroy it, they weaken it, and inevitably, when its strength weakens, it cannot resist diseases.

The physician of hearts, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, said:

*I have seen that sins kill the hearts,*
*and that habitual indulgence in them brings humiliation.*

*And abandoning sins is the life of hearts,*
*and disobeying them is better for your soul.*

**(Fa'ida)**

The disagreement over whether Aisha is superior to Fatimah, or Fatimah is superior.

When the point of comparison is clarified, the matter becomes one of agreement, for preference without distinction is not sound. If by excellence is meant the abundance of reward with God, the Mighty and Majestic, that is a matter known only through a textual proof, because it depends on the relative excellence of the deeds of the hearts, not merely the deeds of the limbs. How many are two doers, one of whom does more with his limbs, while the other has a higher rank than him in Paradise?

If by preference is meant superiority in knowledge, there is no doubt that Aisha was more knowledgeable and more beneficial to the community. She conveyed to the community knowledge that no other conveyed, and both the elite and common of the community were in need of her.

If by preference is meant nobility of lineage and greatness of descent, there is no doubt that Fatimah is superior, for she is a part of the Prophet (ﷺ). That is a distinction in which none shared with her except her sisters.

If by preference is meant leadership, then Fatimah is the leader of the women of the community.

When the aspects of preference, the grounds of excellence and its causes are established, the discussion becomes one of knowledge and justice.

Most people, when they speak about preference, do not distinguish the aspects of excellence, nor do they weigh them against one another, so they diminish the truth. If to that is added a kind of partisanship and desire for the one they favour, they speak with ignorance and injustice.

**(Latifah, a subtle point)**

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah was asked about Khadijah and Aisha, the mothers of the believers, may Allah be pleased with them both: which of them is superior?

He answered that the precedence of Khadijah, her influence at the beginning of Islam, her support and her standing for the religion, were not shared with her by Aisha or any other mother of the believers.

And the influence of Aisha at the end of Islam, her bearing the religion and conveying it to the community, and her attainment of knowledge that Khadijah did not share with her, nor any other, are what distinguished her from others.

Reflect upon this answer, for if you gave any other answer of unqualified preference, you would not escape objection.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verse 36:

When a ruling, whether a command or a statement of fact, has been established from Allah and His Messenger on any matter, it is not permissible for anyone to choose for himself something other than that ruling and go to it instead. This is not permissible for any believing man or woman at all, and so it shows that such conduct is incompatible with faith.

(Section)

The point is that in proportion to one's following of the Messenger there comes honour, sufficiency and victory, just as in proportion to following him there comes guidance, success and salvation. Allah, glory be to Him, has tied the happiness of both abodes to following him, and has placed the misery of both abodes in opposing him. For his followers there is guidance, security, success, honour, sufficiency, victory, support, divine assistance, a good life in this world and the Hereafter. For those who oppose him there is humiliation, abasement, fear, misguidance, forsaking and wretchedness in this world and the Hereafter.

The Prophet (ﷺ) swore that "None of you truly believes until he loves me more than his child, his parent and all of mankind." Allah, glory be to Him, also swore that no one truly believes unless he makes him (the Messenger) the judge in every matter of dispute between himself and others, then is content with his judgment, finds no discomfort within himself regarding what he has decided, and then submits to it fully and yields to it completely. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ [al-Ahzab: 36].

So Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, cut off choice after His command and the command of His Messenger. Thus no believer may choose anything after the command of the Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, when he commands, his command is binding. Choice exists only in the statement of someone other than him when his command is not clear, and that other person is among the people of knowledge concerning him and his Sunnah. With these conditions, the statement of another becomes permissible to follow, but not obligatory to follow. No one is obliged to follow the words of anyone other than him; at most it is permissible for a person to follow such a scholar, and if he leaves the view of another, he is not disobeying Allah and His Messenger.

Where, then, is this compared with one whom all the accountable must follow, whose opposition is forbidden to them, and who must be preferred over every other statement? There is no ruling alongside him, no statement alongside him, just as there is no legislation alongside him. Everyone else, his words are binding only insofar as he commands what he commanded and forbids what he forbade. Thus he was a pure conveyor and informant, not an originator and founder. Whoever originates statements and establishes rules according to his own understanding and interpretation, the Ummah is not obliged to follow them or to refer disputes to them until they are presented to what the Messenger brought. If they agree with it, conform to it and are testified to be sound, they are then accepted. If they oppose it, they must be rejected and discarded. If it is not clear which of the two applies, they are held in abeyance, and the best that can be said of them is that it is permissible to rule or issue fatwas according to them, and permissible to refrain. As for saying that it is obligatory or that they are binding, no, and never.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verse 37:

As for the story of Zaynab bint Jahsh: Zayd had resolved to divorce her, and she did not agree with him. He would consult the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about separating from her, and he (ﷺ) would order him to keep her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ knew that he would certainly separate from her, so he concealed in himself that he would marry her once Zayd had divorced her. He feared the saying of the people: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has married his son's wife," for he had adopted Zayd before prophethood. The Lord, exalted is He, wanted to legislate a general law that contained the interests of His servants. When Zayd divorced her and her waiting period (ʿiddah) from him had ended, He sent him (ﷺ) to her to propose to her for himself. Zayd came and turned his back to the door, and the mention of her by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ weighed heavily on his chest. He called to her from behind the door: "O Zaynab, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is proposing to you." She said: "I will do nothing until I consult my Lord," and she stood at her place of worship and prayed. Allah, mighty and majestic, Himself arranged her marriage to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and concluded the marriage for him above His Throne, and the revelation came with that: ﴿So when Zayd had no further need of her, We married her to you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then rose at once and entered upon her. She used to boast over the wives of the Prophet ﷺ about this, saying: "Your guardians married you off, but Allah married me from above seven heavens." This is the story of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Zaynab.

There is no doubt that the Prophet ﷺ had been made to love women, as in the Sahih from Anas, from him ﷺ:

"Women and perfume have been made beloved to me of your world, and the coolness of my eye has been placed in prayer."

This is the wording of the hadith, not what some narrate: "Three things have been made beloved to me of your world."

Imam Ahmad added in Kitab al-Zuhd to this hadith: "I endure patiently (abstaining) from food and drink, but I cannot endure patiently (abstaining) from them."

The enemies of Allah, the Jews, envied him for this and said: "His only concern is marriage." So Allah, glorified is He, repelled this from His Messenger ﷺ and defended him, saying: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom﴾ [al-Nisa: 54].

[Section: His ﷺ guidance in treating ʿishq (passionate love)]

This is a disease of the heart, differing from all other diseases in its essence, its causes and its treatment. When it becomes firmly established, its cure becomes difficult for physicians, and its affliction exhausts the patient. Allah, glorified is He, related it in His Book concerning two groups of people: women, and lovers of beardless boys. He related it concerning the wife of the ʿAziz regarding Yusuf, and He related it concerning the people of Lut. He, exalted is He, said, informing about them when the angels came to Lut: ﴿And the people of the city came rejoicing (67). He said: Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me (68). And fear Allah and do not humiliate me (69). They said: Did we not forbid you from the worlds? (70). He said: These are my daughters, if you are to act (71). By your life, indeed they were wandering blindly in their intoxication (72).﴾

As for what was claimed by one who did not esteem the Messenger of Allah ﷺ its proper esteem, that he was tested with it regarding Zaynab bint Jahsh, and that he saw her and said: "Glory be to the Turner of hearts," and she captivated his heart, and he began saying to Zayd ibn Harithah: "Keep her," until Allah revealed to him: ﴿And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour: Keep your wife and fear Allah, and you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].

This claimant thought that this was about passionate love. Some of them composed a book on passionate love and mentioned in it the "love" of the prophets, and mentioned this incident. This comes from the ignorance of this speaker regarding the Qur'an and the Messengers, and from his imposing upon the words of Allah what they cannot bear, and attributing to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what Allah has cleared him of. For Zaynab bint Jahsh was under Zayd ibn Harithah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had adopted him, and he was called Zayd ibn Muhammad. Zaynab had a haughtiness and a superiority over him, so he consulted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about divorcing her, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: ﴿Keep your wife and fear Allah﴾, while he concealed within himself that he would marry her if Zayd divorced her. He feared the people's talk that he had married his son's wife, since Zayd was called his son. This is what he concealed in himself, and this is the fear of people that befell him.

For this reason, He, glorified is He, mentioned this verse enumerating His blessings upon him, not rebuking him in it. He informed him that it was not fitting for him to fear people regarding what Allah had made lawful for him, and that Allah has more right that he fear Him. So he should not hesitate to take what Allah made lawful for him because of people's talk. Then He informed him that He, glorified is He, married her to him after Zayd had finished his need of her, so that his community might follow him in that, and that a man may marry the wife of his adopted son, not the wife of his biological son. For this reason He said in the verse of prohibition: ﴿And the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾ [al-Nisa: 23].

He said in this surah: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [al-Ahzab: 40], and He said at its beginning: ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons. That is your saying by your mouths﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4].

So reflect on this defence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the repelling of the attacks of those who assail him. And success is from Allah.

Yes, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved his wives, and the most beloved of them to him was ʿAishah, may Allah be pleased with her. His love for her, or for anyone other than his Lord, never reached the utmost limit of love. Indeed it is established that he said: "Had I been taking a khalil (intimate friend) from among the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a khalil." And in another wording: "Indeed, your companion is the khalil of the Most Merciful."

[Section: Among the first to embrace Islam were ʿAli and Zayd]

ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, hastened to Islam, and he was eight years old, and it was said: more than that. He was under the care of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whom he had taken from his uncle Abu Talib as an aid to him in a year of drought.

"Zayd ibn Harithah, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, hastened to Islam. He had been a slave of Khadijah, and she gave him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when she married him. His father and his uncle came seeking his ransom, and they asked about the Prophet ﷺ, and it was said: he is in the mosque. So they entered upon him and said: "O son of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, O son of Hashim, O son of the chief of his people, you are the people of the Sanctuary of Allah and its neighbours; you free the captive and feed the prisoner. We have come to you about our son who is with you; be gracious to us and be kind to us in his ransom." He said: "And who is he?" They said: "Zayd ibn Harithah." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Would you not have something other than that?" They said: "What is it?" He said: "I will call him and let him choose. If he chooses you, he is yours, and if he chooses me, then by Allah I will not choose anyone over the one who has chosen me." They said: "You have treated us fairly and done well." So he called him and said: "Do you recognise these people?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Who is this?" He said: "This is my father, and this is my uncle." He said: "I am the one you know and have seen, and you have recognised my companionship with you, so choose me or choose them." He said: "I will never choose anyone over you, ever. You are to me in the place of a father and an uncle." They said: "Woe to you, O Zayd! Would you choose slavery over freedom, and over your father and your uncle and your household?" He said: "Yes. I have seen from this man something; I will never choose anyone over him, ever." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw that, he took him out to the Hijr and said: "I call you to witness that Zayd is my son; he inherits from me and I inherit from him." When his father and uncle saw that, their hearts were content, and they departed. He was called Zayd ibn Muhammad until Allah brought Islam, and then the verse was revealed: ﴿Call them by their fathers' names﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5].

So from that day he was called: Zayd ibn Harithah."

Ma'mar said in his "Jami'" from al-Zuhri: "We do not know of anyone who embraced Islam before Zayd ibn Harithah, and he is the one about whom Allah informed in His Book that He bestowed favour upon him, and His Messenger bestowed favour upon him, and He mentioned him by his name."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verses 41–43 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Jawhari said: *al-asil* (the late afternoon) is the time after the 'asr (afternoon) prayer until the maghrib (sunset). Its plural is *asl*, *aasal* and *asa'il*, as if it were *asila*.

The poet said:
"By my life, you are the house, honoring its people,
and I sit in its shade in the evenings."

It is also pluralized as *asjlan*, like *ba'ir* and *ba'ran* (camel and camels). Then they formed the diminutive of the plural, saying *asaylan*, then they replaced the final *n* with *l* and said *asaylal*.

The poet said:
"I stood there a while (*usaylalan*), asking it,
it could not answer, and there was no one in the abode."

**(Benefit)**

Among those who remember God are some who begin with the tongue, even while heedless, and then do not cease until the heart is present, so that the tongue and the heart agree in the remembrance. And among them are those who do not see this and do not begin in heedlessness, but remain still until the heart is present, and then begin the remembrance with the heart. When that grows strong, it draws the tongue along, and both agree together. The first one moves the remembrance from the tongue to the heart, and the second moves it from the heart to the tongue, without his heart ever being empty of it. Rather, he remains still at first until he senses the speaker manifesting within him. When he senses that, his heart speaks, then the inner speech passes into the outer remembrance of the tongue, and he then becomes immersed in it until he finds every part of himself remembering. The best and most beneficial remembrance is that in which the heart agrees with the tongue, that which is from the prophetic supplications, and in which the one remembering witnesses its meanings and purposes.

**[Chapter on the Station of Remembrance]**

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is the station of remembrance (*dhikr*). It is the great station of the people (the spiritual travelers), from which they take provisions, in which they trade, and to which they constantly return.

Remembrance is the banner of sovereignty (*wilaya*): whoever is given it is connected, and whoever is denied it is dismissed. It is the nourishment of the hearts of these people; when it leaves them, bodies become graves for them. It is the cultivation of their abodes, which, when left idle of it, become wasteland. It is their weapon, with which they fight the highway robbers, and their water, with which they extinguish the blazing of the path, and the cure for their ailments, when it departs from them, hearts relapse. It is the connecting cause and the bond that existed between them and the Knower of the unseen.

*"When we fall ill, we are treated by remembering you,*
*so we leave remembrance at times, and so we relapse."*

By it they ward off calamities, remove distresses, and by it hardships become easy for them. When trial overshadows them, to it is their refuge, and when calamities descend upon them, to it is their recourse. It is the gardens of their paradise in which they move about, and the capital of their happiness with which they trade. It leaves the sorrowful heart laughing and joyful, it brings the one who remembers to the One remembered, and indeed it leaves the one who remembers as one who is remembered.

In every limb there is a time-bound worship, but remembrance is the worship of the heart and the tongue, and it is not time-bound. Rather, they are commanded to remember their Worshipped and Beloved at all times: ﴿standing, sitting and on their sides﴾. Just as paradise is a barren plain and remembrance is its planting, so the hearts are wasteland and ruin, and remembrance is their cultivation and foundation.

It is the polish and burnish of hearts, and their medicine when illness overtakes them. Whenever the one who remembers increases in his remembrance, his immersion grows, and the One remembered becomes more beloved to him, and his longing for meeting Him increases. When his heart agrees with his tongue in remembrance, he forgets everything in the presence of that remembrance, God preserves everything for him, and it becomes a substitute for everything.

By it, deafness is removed from the ears, muteness from the tongues, and darkness is dispelled from the eyes. God adorns the tongues of those who remember with it, just as He adorns the sight of onlookers with light. So the heedless tongue is like a blind eye, a deaf ear and a paralyzed hand.

It is the greatest door of God, open between Him and His servant, so long as the servant does not close it through his heedlessness.

Al-Hasan al-Basri (may God have mercy on him) said: "Seek sweetness in three things: in the prayer, in remembrance, and in the recitation of the Qur'an. If you find it, well; if not, know that the door is closed."

Through remembrance, the servant overthrows Satan, just as Satan overthrows those who are heedless and forgetful.

One of the early generations (*salaf*) said: "When remembrance takes firm hold of the heart, if Satan approaches it, he is thrown down, just as a person is thrown down when Satan approaches him. Then the devils gather around him and say: 'What is wrong with this one?' It is said to them: 'The human has touched him.'"

It is the spirit of righteous deeds: when a deed is empty of remembrance, it is like a body without a spirit. And God knows best.

**[Chapter on the Aspects of Remembrance in the Qur'an]**

It appears in the Qur'an in ten aspects.

The first: the command to it, absolute and restricted.
The second: the prohibition of its opposite, heedlessness and forgetfulness.
The third: linking success (*falah*) to its continuity and abundance.
The fourth: praise of its people and the report of what God has prepared for them of paradise and forgiveness.
The fifth: the report of the loss of those who are diverted from it by other things.
The sixth: that He, glory be to Him, made His remembrance of them a reward for their remembrance of Him.
The seventh: the report that it is greater than everything.
The eighth: that He made it the seal of righteous deeds, just as it was their key.
The ninth: the report about its people that they are the ones who benefit from His signs, and that they alone are the people of understanding (*ulu al-albab*), to the exclusion of others.
The tenth: that He made it the companion of all righteous deeds and their spirit, so that when you lack it, they are like a body without a spirit.

**[Details of the Aspects of Remembrance in the Qur'an]**

A chapter on the explanation of these.

1. As for the first, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, remember God with frequent remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening. It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out of darkness into light. And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41–43], and His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear﴾ [al-A'raf: 205].

On this there are two views: one, that it is in your secret self and heart; the other, that it is with your tongue, in such a way that you hear yourself.

2. As for the prohibition of its opposite, it is like His saying: ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾ [al-A'raf: 205], and His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot God, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [al-Hashr: 19].

3. As for linking success to its abundance, it is like His saying: ﴿And remember God much, that you may be successful﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

4. As for praise of its people and the goodness of their recompense, it is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women…﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35], up to His saying: ﴿and the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him much, God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

5. As for the loss of those diverted from it, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that, they are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

6. As for His making His remembrance of them a reward for their remembrance of Him, it is like His saying: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152].

7. As for the report that it is greater than everything, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. And the remembrance of God is greater﴾ [al-Ankabut: 45]. On this there are four views:

One: that the remembrance of God is greater than everything, so it is the best of acts of worship, because the purpose of all acts of worship is to establish His remembrance; it is the secret and spirit of worship.

The second: the meaning is that when you remember Him, He remembers you, so His remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. According to this, the verbal noun (*masdar*) is attributed to the agent; according to the first, it is attributed to the object remembered.

The third: the meaning is that the remembrance of God is too great to let indecency and wrongdoing remain with it; rather, when the remembrance is complete, it erases every sin and disobedience. This is what the exegetes (*mufassirun*) have mentioned.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may God have mercy on him) say: The meaning of the verse is that prayer has two great benefits. One is that it prohibits indecency and wrongdoing. The second is that it includes the remembrance of God and contains Him and what it contains of the remembrance of God is greater than its prohibition of indecency and wrongdoing.

8. As for the sealing of righteous deeds with it: just as the act of fasting is sealed with His saying: ﴿and that you complete the period, and that you glorify God for having guided you, and that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].

Hajj is sealed with it in His saying: ﴿So when you have completed your rites, remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 200].

The prayer is sealed with it, as in His saying: ﴿So when you have completed the prayer, remember God standing, sitting and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103]. And the Friday prayer is sealed with it, as in His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of God's bounty, and remember God much that you may be successful﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

For this reason, it is the seal of the worldly life, and if it is the last word of a servant, God admits him into paradise.

9. As for the restriction of those who remember to benefiting from His signs, and they are the people of understanding and intellect, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding, who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190–191].

10. As for its companionship with all deeds, its being joined to them, and that it is their spirit: He, glory be to Him, joined it with the prayer, as in His saying: ﴿And establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ [Ta-Ha: 14]. He joined it with fasting and with Hajj and its rites; indeed, it is the spirit, core and purpose of Hajj. As the Prophet said: "The circling of the House, the running between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and the stoning of the pillars were only prescribed for the establishment of the remembrance of God."

He joined it with jihad, and commanded remembering Him when meeting opponents and confronting enemies, saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much, that you may be successful﴾ [al-Anfal: 45].

In a divine report, God says: "Indeed My servant, every one of My servants, who remembers Me while he is meeting his opponent…"

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may God sanctify his soul) cite it as evidence, and I heard him say: Lovers take pride in mentioning the one they love in this state, as 'Antarah said:

*"I remembered you while the spears were like*
*ropes of a well in the chest of a dark horse."*

Another said:

*"I remembered you while the spear swayed between us,*
*and the close-set dark spears had already drunk from us."*

Another said:

*"I remembered you while the spears were splintering,*
*holding, and the Indian swords dripped with my blood."*

This is abundant in their poetry, and it indicates the strength of love. For the lover's remembrance of his beloved in that state, when a man is concerned with nothing but himself, indicates that the beloved is for him in the position of his own self or dearer than it, and this is a proof of the sincerity of love. And God knows best.

**[Chapter on the Excellence of the People of Remembrance]**

Those who remember are the foremost, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of God was traveling on the road to Makkah when he passed a mountain called Jumdan, and said: 'Go on, this is Jumdan; the solitary ones (*al-mufarridun*) have outstripped.' They said: 'And who are the solitary ones, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'Those who remember God much, men and women.'" The *mufarridun* are either the monotheists (*al-muwahhidun*) or those who are alone and single.

In the Musnad, there is a raised (*marfu'*) hadith from Abu al-Darda' (may God be pleased with him): "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest in the sight of your King, the highest in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike yours?" They said: "And what is that, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The remembrance of God, mighty and majestic."

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Aghar say: "I testify concerning Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id (may God be pleased with them both) that they both bore witness concerning the Messenger of God that he said: 'No people sit remembering God except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and God mentions them among those who are with Him.'" This is in Sahih Muslim.

It suffices for the honor of remembrance that God boasts of its people to His angels, as in Sahih Muslim from Mu'awiyah (may God be pleased with him): "The Messenger of God went out to a circle of his companions and said: 'What has made you sit?' They said: 'We sat remembering God and praising Him for having guided us to Islam and bestowed it upon us.' He said: 'By God, did nothing but that make you sit?' They said: 'By God, nothing but that made us sit.' He said: 'As for me, I did not ask you to swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibril came to me and informed me that God boasts of you to the angels.'"

A Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deeds are the best?" He said: "That you depart this world while your tongue is still moist with the remembrance of Allah." A man said to him: "The laws of Islam have become too many for me, so instruct me in one thing that I may hold fast to." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah."

In the Musnad and elsewhere, from the hadith of Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah came out to us and said: 'O people, graze in the gardens of Paradise!' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?' He said: 'The gatherings of dhikr.'"

He (ﷺ) also said: "Go out in the morning, return in the evening, and remember (Allah). Whoever wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him look at Allah's standing with him, for Allah lowers the servant to the place where He has lowered him in His own regard."

The Prophet (ﷺ) related from his father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), that he said to him: "Convey my greetings of peace to your community and inform them that Paradise has pure soil and sweet water, that it is a level plain (qi'an), and that its planting is: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad and others.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The likeness of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not remember Him is the likeness of the living and the dead." The wording of Muslim is: "The likeness of the house in which Allah is remembered and the house in which Allah is not remembered is the likeness of the living and the dead." Thus he made the house of the one who remembers like the house of the living, and the house of the heedless like the house of the dead, which is the grave.

In the first wording, he made the one who remembers like the living and the heedless like the dead. Both wordings thus imply that the heart that remembers is like one living among the dwellings of the living, and the heedless heart is like one dead among the dwellings of the dead. There is no doubt that the bodies of the heedless are graves for their hearts, and their hearts within them are like the dead in graves, as it has been said:

*Forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah is the death of their hearts,*
*and their bodies, before the graves, are graves.*

*And their spirits are in loneliness away from their bodies,*
*and for them there is no resurrection until the Resurrection.*

And as it has been said:

*Forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah is the death of their hearts,*
*and their bodies are the effaced graves.*

*And their spirits are in loneliness away from their Beloved,*
*yet they are companions of the wicked.*

In a divine report: "Allah the Exalted says: 'When the remembrance of Me prevails over My servant, he loves Me and I love him.'"

In another: "'So rejoice in Me, and find delight in My remembrance.'"

In another: "'Son of Adam, you have not been fair to Me! I remember you while you forget Me; I call you while you flee to other than Me. I remove your afflictions while you are absorbed in your sins. Son of Adam, what will you say tomorrow when you come to Me?'"

In another: "'Son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry: I will remember you when I am angry. Be content with My help for you, for My help for you is better than your help for yourself.'"

In the Sahih, in the report that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrates from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs."

We have mentioned about one hundred benefits of dhikr in our book *al-Wabil al-Sayyib wa Rafi' al-Kalim al-Tayyib* (The Heavy Rain and the Good Word that Ascends), and we mentioned there the secrets of dhikr, its great benefit and its excellent fruit. There we also mentioned that dhikr is of three kinds: the remembrance of the Names and Attributes and their meanings, praising Allah by them, and affirming the Oneness of Allah through them;

the remembrance of the command and prohibition, and of the lawful and the unlawful;

and the remembrance of Allah's favours, blessings and kindnesses.

It is also of three kinds: remembrance in which the heart and the tongue agree, which is the highest; remembrance by the heart alone, which is in the second rank; and remembrance by the bare tongue, which is in the third rank.

[Degrees of Dhikr]

[The First Degree: Outward Dhikr]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree is outward dhikr, which consists of praise, supplication or watchfulness.

By "outward" he means that which flows upon the tongue and corresponds to the heart, not mere tongue-movement, for the people of this path do not regard the latter as counting.

As for the remembrance of praise, it is like: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar. As for the remembrance of supplication, it is like: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers" (al-A'raf 7:23), and: "O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek help," and the like.

As for the remembrance of watchfulness, it is like the speaker's saying: "Allah is with me, Allah is watching me, Allah is my witness," and the like, which is used to strengthen presence with Allah. In it is the safeguarding of the good of the heart, the preservation of courtesy toward Allah, guarding against heedlessness, and seeking protection from Satan and the self.

The prophetic adhkar (remembrances) combine all three kinds, for they include praise of Allah, an opening for supplication and request, and an explicit statement of it, as in the hadith: "The best supplication is al-hamdu lillah." It was said to Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: "How did he make it a supplication?" He said: "Have you not heard the words of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt to Abd Allah ibn Jud'an, hoping for his gift:

*Shall I mention my need, or has your modesty sufficed me?*
*Your modesty is indeed your nature.*

*When a man praises you one day,*
*his praise suffices him from asking you.*"

So this is a created being who was content, from another created being, with praise of him instead of a request. How then is it with the Lord of the worlds?

The prophetic adhkar also include the fullness of watchfulness, the good of the heart, guarding against heedlessness, and seeking protection from distracting thoughts and Satan. And Allah knows best.

[Section: The Second Degree: Hidden Dhikr]

He said: The second degree is hidden dhikr, which is deliverance from fetters, remaining in witnessing (shuhud), and constant intimate conversation (musamara).

By "hidden" here he means remembrance by the heart alone, with whatever arises in it of inspirations (waridat), and this is the fruit of the first dhikr.

By "deliverance from fetters" he means being freed from heedlessness, forgetfulness and the veils that stand between the heart and the Lord, glorified is He. "Remaining in witnessing" means persisting in presence with the One remembered, and the heart witnessing Him until it is as if it sees Him.

"Constant intimate conversation" is the heart's ongoing private address to its Lord: sometimes in humble flattery, sometimes in lowly supplication, sometimes in praise, sometimes in glorification, and other kinds of secret and inward communion. This is the condition of every lover with his beloved, as it has been said:

*When we are alone, with the watcher present in the gathering,*
*we are silent, while desire speaks.*

[Section: The Third Degree: Real Dhikr]

He said: The third degree is real dhikr, which is witnessing the Real's remembrance of you, and being freed from witnessing your own remembrance, and recognising the pretence of the one who remembers in his remaining with the remembrance.

This remembrance in this degree is called "real" only because it is ascribed to the Lord, exalted is He. As for the ascription of remembrance to the servant, it is not real. Thus Allah's remembrance of His servant is the real remembrance, and it is witnessing that the Real remembers His servant, and remembers him among those whom He has singled out and qualified for nearness to Him and for His remembrance. So He made him one who remembers Him. In truth, He is the one who remembers Himself, by making His servant remember Him and by qualifying him for His remembrance. This meaning is what he alluded to in the chapter on Tawhid (Oneness) with his saying:

*His affirming of Himself is His affirming (of Oneness),*
*and the description of one who describes Him is a heretic's.*

That is, He is the one who in truth affirmed His own Oneness, so the servant's affirmation of Oneness is ascribed to Him in truth, and its ascription to the servant is not real.

For the servant, in that state, was neither by himself nor from himself; rather, he is placed in him. If he is called one who affirms Oneness and one who remembers, it is because he is the channel and locus of what flows in him, just as one is called white, black, tall or short because he is the locus of these attributes, having no making in them. His will did not bring them about, nor his power, nor his strength. This goes along with what accompanies it of being overwhelmed by nearness and by annihilation from the trace (rasm), and of absence through the witnessed from witnessing, and the strength of the inspiration. From this is composed a special taste: that no one affirmed Allah's Oneness except Allah, no one remembered Allah except Allah, and no one loved Allah except Allah.

This is the reality of what the people of this path hold. The knowers among them, the masters of insight, gave with this their due to servitude and their due to knowledge, and recognised that the servant is truly a servant in every respect, and the Lord is truly a Lord in every respect. They fulfilled the right of servitude through Allah, not through themselves, and for Allah, not for their own portions. They passed away in witnessing the meanings of His Names and Attributes from all else, and in what He loves and is pleased with, from what is accomplished by His will and decree. For the whole of existence is by Him, and what is His, namely His beloved and what pleases Him, is for Him and by Him. As for those who deviated, they passed away in what is by Him from what is for Him; so they took as allies His enemies, abandoned His religion, and equated His loves with His hatreds and the places of His pleasure with the places of His anger. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

His saying "recognising the pretence" means: by the annihilation of witnessing His remembrance of you from witnessing your remembrance of Him. This witnessing relieves the servant from seeing the self and from observing his own deeds, and it causes him to die and to live: it causes him to die to himself, and to live through his Lord; it annihilates him and separates him from himself and connects him to his Lord. This is the very attainment of victory over the self.

One of the knowers said: "The journey of the seekers ends in victory over their selves."

His saying "and recognising the pretence of the one who remembers in his remaining with the remembrance" means: the one who remains with the remembrance bears witness against himself that he is the one who remembers, and that is a pretence on his part, for he has no action of his own. This pretence does not leave him except when he passes away from his remembrance, for witnessing his own remembrance and remaining with it is a pretence that includes ascribing the remembrance to himself, while in truth it is not his.

It may be said: Glory be to Allah! What pretence is there in this? Is this not witnessing the realities as they are? For when he witnesses himself remembering, by Allah's making him one who remembers and His qualifying him for it, and by the remembrance of Allah coming before the servant's remembrance of Him, then both matters come together in his witnessing. So what pretence is there here? Is this not the very truth and the witnessing of realities as they are?

Yes, pretence is this: that he witnesses that remembrance as coming from himself, by his own power and strength, and not from Allah alone.

However, the Shaykh (the author of the source) is not restrained in annihilation by the blame of any blamer, nor does he listen to any reproacher in it.

What is beyond doubt is that remaining in dhikr is more perfect than annihilation in it and absence through it, because remaining contains detail, knowledge, witnessing realities as they are, and distinguishing between the Lord and the servant, between what subsists in the servant and what subsists in the Lord, exalted is He, and the witnessing of servanthood and the One served. Annihilation contains none of that. Annihilation, by its name, is annihilation, and subsistence is subsistence by its name. Annihilation is sought for something else, while subsistence is sought for its own sake. Annihilation is an attribute of the servant, and subsistence is an attribute of the Lord. Annihilation is non-existence, and subsistence is existence. Annihilation is negation, and subsistence is affirmation. Travelling on the path of annihilation is perilous, and how many deserts and ruins are in it! Travelling on the path of subsistence is safe, for the guides, the leaders and the protectors have trodden it. But the people of annihilation claim that it is a long road, yet they do not doubt its safety and its arrival at the goal. However, they claim that the path of annihilation is shorter, and that its rider flies, while the rider of the path of subsistence walks. The perfect among the travellers see annihilation as one station of the stations of the road, and its alighting is not general for every traveller; rather, some of them do not see it and do not pass by it. The greatest path and the most upright road is the path of subsistence. They argue against the one who is in annihilation by his moving from it to something else, for otherwise he is, in their view, in danger. And Allah is the One whose help is sought, and He, glorified is He, knows best.

(Section: Reading the Qur'an is better than dhikr, and dhikr is better than supplication)

This is considered by looking at each of them in isolation. However, what is less excellent may come to have a ruling that makes it preferable to the more excellent, indeed one that makes it obligatory, so that one may not turn away from it to the more excellent. Such is the glorification in bowing and prostration, for it is better than reciting the Qur'an in them; indeed, reciting in them is forbidden, whether as a prohibition or as a disapproval. Likewise, saying "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him) and "Rabbana wa lakal-hamd" (Our Lord, and to You be praise) in their places are better than recitation. Likewise the tashahhud. Likewise "Rabbi ighfir li, warhamni, wahdini, wa 'afini, warzuqni" (My Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide for me) between the two prostrations is better than recitation. Likewise the dhikr after the salam of the prayer, the remembrance of tahlil, tasbih, takbir and tahmid, is better than occupying oneself with recitation instead of it. Likewise, responding to the muezzin and saying as he says is better than recitation.

The excellence of the Qur'an over every other speech is like the excellence of God Most High over His creation. Yet every situation has its own fitting speech. Whenever the fitting speech is missed and one turns away from it to something else, wisdom is disturbed and the benefit intended from it is lost.

Likewise, beneficial remembrances (adhkar) suited to specific occasions are better than unrestricted recitation, and unrestricted recitation is better than unrestricted remembrances. The exception is when something befalls the servant that makes a remembrance or supplication more beneficial to him than reciting the Qur'an.

An example: he reflects on his sins, and this leads him to repentance through seeking forgiveness (istighfar), or something he fears harm from befalls him, from the devils of mankind and the jinn, so he turns to the remembrances and supplications that fortify and protect him.

Similarly, a servant may face a pressing need, and if he is occupied without asking for it, or with a remembrance in which his heart is not present, but when he turns to asking for it and calling upon God for it, his whole heart gathers upon God Most High and produces in him humility, submission, and earnest entreaty. In that state, his occupation with supplication is more beneficial, even though each of recitation and remembrance is more excellent and greater in reward.

This is a beneficial door that requires a discerning understanding (fiqh nafs) and a distinction (furqan) between the excellence of a thing in itself and its excellence that arises from circumstances. Thus one gives every possessor his right and places everything in its proper place: the eye has its place, the foot has its place, water has its place, and meat has its place.

Preserving the ranks (maratib) is part of the completeness of wisdom, which is the order of command and prohibition.

And God Most High is the Granter of success.

Likewise, soap and alkali (ashnan) are more beneficial for a garment at one time, while fumigation (tajmir), rosewater, and ironing it are more beneficial for it at another time.

One day I said to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may God have mercy on him: Some scholars were asked, "Which is more beneficial for the servant, glorification (tasbih) or seeking forgiveness (istighfar)?" He said: "If the garment is clean, then incense and rosewater are more beneficial for it; if it is soiled, then soap and hot water are more beneficial for it."

He said to me, may God have mercy on him: "How so, when the garments are still soiled?" Among this category is that the surah ﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas] equals one third of the Qur'an, yet with this it does not replace the verses on inheritance, divorce, khul' (divorce initiated by the wife), the waiting period ('iddah), and the like. Rather, those verses at their time and when needed are more beneficial than reciting the surah al-Ikhlas.

Since prayer comprises recitation, remembrance, and supplication, and gathers the components of servitude in the most complete way, it is more excellent than each of recitation, remembrance, and supplication alone, because it combines all of that together with the servitude of all the limbs.
