This is a very beneficial principle that opens for the servant the door of knowing the ranks of deeds and placing them in their proper stations, so that he does not occupy himself with the lesser from the greater, thereby letting Iblis win the excess that lies between them, or look at the greater and occupy himself with it at the expense of the lesser when that is the time for the lesser, so that its benefit is entirely lost, supposing that his occupation with the greater yields more reward and greater recompense.

This requires knowledge of the ranks of deeds, their differences and purposes, and understanding in giving each deed its right and placing it in its rank, and in preferring what is more important over it, or forgoing what is superior and more excellent when it can be made up for and returned to. As for a lesser deed whose time, if missed, cannot be made up, then occupying oneself with it is preferable. An example of this is leaving recitation to return a greeting (radd al-salam) or to say "may God have mercy on you" to one who sneezes (tashmit al-atis), even though the Qur'an is more excellent, because he can occupy himself with this lesser act and then return to the greater; whereas if he occupies himself with recitation, he misses the benefit of returning the greeting and of saying "may God have mercy on you" to the sneezer. Likewise all deeds when they compete.

And God Most High is the Granter of success.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verses 41–43 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Jawhari said: *al-asil* (the late afternoon) is the time after the 'asr (afternoon) prayer until the maghrib (sunset). Its plural is *asl*, *aasal* and *asa'il*, as if it were *asila*.

The poet said:
"By my life, you are the house, honoring its people,
and I sit in its shade in the evenings."

It is also pluralized as *asjlan*, like *ba'ir* and *ba'ran* (camel and camels). Then they formed the diminutive of the plural, saying *asaylan*, then they replaced the final *n* with *l* and said *asaylal*.

The poet said:
"I stood there a while (*usaylalan*), asking it,
it could not answer, and there was no one in the abode."

**(Benefit)**

Among those who remember God are some who begin with the tongue, even while heedless, and then do not cease until the heart is present, so that the tongue and the heart agree in the remembrance. And among them are those who do not see this and do not begin in heedlessness, but remain still until the heart is present, and then begin the remembrance with the heart. When that grows strong, it draws the tongue along, and both agree together. The first one moves the remembrance from the tongue to the heart, and the second moves it from the heart to the tongue, without his heart ever being empty of it. Rather, he remains still at first until he senses the speaker manifesting within him. When he senses that, his heart speaks, then the inner speech passes into the outer remembrance of the tongue, and he then becomes immersed in it until he finds every part of himself remembering. The best and most beneficial remembrance is that in which the heart agrees with the tongue, that which is from the prophetic supplications, and in which the one remembering witnesses its meanings and purposes.

**[Chapter on the Station of Remembrance]**

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is the station of remembrance (*dhikr*). It is the great station of the people (the spiritual travelers), from which they take provisions, in which they trade, and to which they constantly return.

Remembrance is the banner of sovereignty (*wilaya*): whoever is given it is connected, and whoever is denied it is dismissed. It is the nourishment of the hearts of these people; when it leaves them, bodies become graves for them. It is the cultivation of their abodes, which, when left idle of it, become wasteland. It is their weapon, with which they fight the highway robbers, and their water, with which they extinguish the blazing of the path, and the cure for their ailments, when it departs from them, hearts relapse. It is the connecting cause and the bond that existed between them and the Knower of the unseen.

*"When we fall ill, we are treated by remembering you,*
*so we leave remembrance at times, and so we relapse."*

By it they ward off calamities, remove distresses, and by it hardships become easy for them. When trial overshadows them, to it is their refuge, and when calamities descend upon them, to it is their recourse. It is the gardens of their paradise in which they move about, and the capital of their happiness with which they trade. It leaves the sorrowful heart laughing and joyful, it brings the one who remembers to the One remembered, and indeed it leaves the one who remembers as one who is remembered.

In every limb there is a time-bound worship, but remembrance is the worship of the heart and the tongue, and it is not time-bound. Rather, they are commanded to remember their Worshipped and Beloved at all times: ﴿standing, sitting and on their sides﴾. Just as paradise is a barren plain and remembrance is its planting, so the hearts are wasteland and ruin, and remembrance is their cultivation and foundation.

It is the polish and burnish of hearts, and their medicine when illness overtakes them. Whenever the one who remembers increases in his remembrance, his immersion grows, and the One remembered becomes more beloved to him, and his longing for meeting Him increases. When his heart agrees with his tongue in remembrance, he forgets everything in the presence of that remembrance, God preserves everything for him, and it becomes a substitute for everything.

By it, deafness is removed from the ears, muteness from the tongues, and darkness is dispelled from the eyes. God adorns the tongues of those who remember with it, just as He adorns the sight of onlookers with light. So the heedless tongue is like a blind eye, a deaf ear and a paralyzed hand.

It is the greatest door of God, open between Him and His servant, so long as the servant does not close it through his heedlessness.

Al-Hasan al-Basri (may God have mercy on him) said: "Seek sweetness in three things: in the prayer, in remembrance, and in the recitation of the Qur'an. If you find it, well; if not, know that the door is closed."

Through remembrance, the servant overthrows Satan, just as Satan overthrows those who are heedless and forgetful.

One of the early generations (*salaf*) said: "When remembrance takes firm hold of the heart, if Satan approaches it, he is thrown down, just as a person is thrown down when Satan approaches him. Then the devils gather around him and say: 'What is wrong with this one?' It is said to them: 'The human has touched him.'"

It is the spirit of righteous deeds: when a deed is empty of remembrance, it is like a body without a spirit. And God knows best.

**[Chapter on the Aspects of Remembrance in the Qur'an]**

It appears in the Qur'an in ten aspects.

The first: the command to it, absolute and restricted.
The second: the prohibition of its opposite, heedlessness and forgetfulness.
The third: linking success (*falah*) to its continuity and abundance.
The fourth: praise of its people and the report of what God has prepared for them of paradise and forgiveness.
The fifth: the report of the loss of those who are diverted from it by other things.
The sixth: that He, glory be to Him, made His remembrance of them a reward for their remembrance of Him.
The seventh: the report that it is greater than everything.
The eighth: that He made it the seal of righteous deeds, just as it was their key.
The ninth: the report about its people that they are the ones who benefit from His signs, and that they alone are the people of understanding (*ulu al-albab*), to the exclusion of others.
The tenth: that He made it the companion of all righteous deeds and their spirit, so that when you lack it, they are like a body without a spirit.

**[Details of the Aspects of Remembrance in the Qur'an]**

A chapter on the explanation of these.

1. As for the first, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, remember God with frequent remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening. It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out of darkness into light. And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41–43], and His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear﴾ [al-A'raf: 205].

On this there are two views: one, that it is in your secret self and heart; the other, that it is with your tongue, in such a way that you hear yourself.

2. As for the prohibition of its opposite, it is like His saying: ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾ [al-A'raf: 205], and His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot God, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [al-Hashr: 19].

3. As for linking success to its abundance, it is like His saying: ﴿And remember God much, that you may be successful﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

4. As for praise of its people and the goodness of their recompense, it is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women…﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35], up to His saying: ﴿and the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him much, God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

5. As for the loss of those diverted from it, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that, they are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

6. As for His making His remembrance of them a reward for their remembrance of Him, it is like His saying: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152].

7. As for the report that it is greater than everything, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. And the remembrance of God is greater﴾ [al-Ankabut: 45]. On this there are four views:

One: that the remembrance of God is greater than everything, so it is the best of acts of worship, because the purpose of all acts of worship is to establish His remembrance; it is the secret and spirit of worship.

The second: the meaning is that when you remember Him, He remembers you, so His remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. According to this, the verbal noun (*masdar*) is attributed to the agent; according to the first, it is attributed to the object remembered.

The third: the meaning is that the remembrance of God is too great to let indecency and wrongdoing remain with it; rather, when the remembrance is complete, it erases every sin and disobedience. This is what the exegetes (*mufassirun*) have mentioned.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may God have mercy on him) say: The meaning of the verse is that prayer has two great benefits. One is that it prohibits indecency and wrongdoing. The second is that it includes the remembrance of God and contains Him and what it contains of the remembrance of God is greater than its prohibition of indecency and wrongdoing.

8. As for the sealing of righteous deeds with it: just as the act of fasting is sealed with His saying: ﴿and that you complete the period, and that you glorify God for having guided you, and that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].

Hajj is sealed with it in His saying: ﴿So when you have completed your rites, remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 200].

The prayer is sealed with it, as in His saying: ﴿So when you have completed the prayer, remember God standing, sitting and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103]. And the Friday prayer is sealed with it, as in His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of God's bounty, and remember God much that you may be successful﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

For this reason, it is the seal of the worldly life, and if it is the last word of a servant, God admits him into paradise.

9. As for the restriction of those who remember to benefiting from His signs, and they are the people of understanding and intellect, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding, who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190–191].

10. As for its companionship with all deeds, its being joined to them, and that it is their spirit: He, glory be to Him, joined it with the prayer, as in His saying: ﴿And establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ [Ta-Ha: 14]. He joined it with fasting and with Hajj and its rites; indeed, it is the spirit, core and purpose of Hajj. As the Prophet said: "The circling of the House, the running between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and the stoning of the pillars were only prescribed for the establishment of the remembrance of God."

He joined it with jihad, and commanded remembering Him when meeting opponents and confronting enemies, saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much, that you may be successful﴾ [al-Anfal: 45].

In a divine report, God says: "Indeed My servant, every one of My servants, who remembers Me while he is meeting his opponent…"

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may God sanctify his soul) cite it as evidence, and I heard him say: Lovers take pride in mentioning the one they love in this state, as 'Antarah said:

*"I remembered you while the spears were like*
*ropes of a well in the chest of a dark horse."*

Another said:

*"I remembered you while the spear swayed between us,*
*and the close-set dark spears had already drunk from us."*

Another said:

*"I remembered you while the spears were splintering,*
*holding, and the Indian swords dripped with my blood."*

This is abundant in their poetry, and it indicates the strength of love. For the lover's remembrance of his beloved in that state, when a man is concerned with nothing but himself, indicates that the beloved is for him in the position of his own self or dearer than it, and this is a proof of the sincerity of love. And God knows best.

**[Chapter on the Excellence of the People of Remembrance]**

Those who remember are the foremost, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of God was traveling on the road to Makkah when he passed a mountain called Jumdan, and said: 'Go on, this is Jumdan; the solitary ones (*al-mufarridun*) have outstripped.' They said: 'And who are the solitary ones, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'Those who remember God much, men and women.'" The *mufarridun* are either the monotheists (*al-muwahhidun*) or those who are alone and single.

In the Musnad, there is a raised (*marfu'*) hadith from Abu al-Darda' (may God be pleased with him): "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest in the sight of your King, the highest in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike yours?" They said: "And what is that, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The remembrance of God, mighty and majestic."

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Aghar say: "I testify concerning Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id (may God be pleased with them both) that they both bore witness concerning the Messenger of God that he said: 'No people sit remembering God except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and God mentions them among those who are with Him.'" This is in Sahih Muslim.

It suffices for the honor of remembrance that God boasts of its people to His angels, as in Sahih Muslim from Mu'awiyah (may God be pleased with him): "The Messenger of God went out to a circle of his companions and said: 'What has made you sit?' They said: 'We sat remembering God and praising Him for having guided us to Islam and bestowed it upon us.' He said: 'By God, did nothing but that make you sit?' They said: 'By God, nothing but that made us sit.' He said: 'As for me, I did not ask you to swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibril came to me and informed me that God boasts of you to the angels.'"

A Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deeds are the best?" He said: "That you depart this world while your tongue is still moist with the remembrance of Allah." A man said to him: "The laws of Islam have become too many for me, so instruct me in one thing that I may hold fast to." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah."

In the Musnad and elsewhere, from the hadith of Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah came out to us and said: 'O people, graze in the gardens of Paradise!' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?' He said: 'The gatherings of dhikr.'"

He (ﷺ) also said: "Go out in the morning, return in the evening, and remember (Allah). Whoever wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him look at Allah's standing with him, for Allah lowers the servant to the place where He has lowered him in His own regard."

The Prophet (ﷺ) related from his father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), that he said to him: "Convey my greetings of peace to your community and inform them that Paradise has pure soil and sweet water, that it is a level plain (qi'an), and that its planting is: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad and others.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The likeness of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not remember Him is the likeness of the living and the dead." The wording of Muslim is: "The likeness of the house in which Allah is remembered and the house in which Allah is not remembered is the likeness of the living and the dead." Thus he made the house of the one who remembers like the house of the living, and the house of the heedless like the house of the dead, which is the grave.

In the first wording, he made the one who remembers like the living and the heedless like the dead. Both wordings thus imply that the heart that remembers is like one living among the dwellings of the living, and the heedless heart is like one dead among the dwellings of the dead. There is no doubt that the bodies of the heedless are graves for their hearts, and their hearts within them are like the dead in graves, as it has been said:

*Forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah is the death of their hearts,*
*and their bodies, before the graves, are graves.*

*And their spirits are in loneliness away from their bodies,*
*and for them there is no resurrection until the Resurrection.*

And as it has been said:

*Forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah is the death of their hearts,*
*and their bodies are the effaced graves.*

*And their spirits are in loneliness away from their Beloved,*
*yet they are companions of the wicked.*

In a divine report: "Allah the Exalted says: 'When the remembrance of Me prevails over My servant, he loves Me and I love him.'"

In another: "'So rejoice in Me, and find delight in My remembrance.'"

In another: "'Son of Adam, you have not been fair to Me! I remember you while you forget Me; I call you while you flee to other than Me. I remove your afflictions while you are absorbed in your sins. Son of Adam, what will you say tomorrow when you come to Me?'"

In another: "'Son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry: I will remember you when I am angry. Be content with My help for you, for My help for you is better than your help for yourself.'"

In the Sahih, in the report that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrates from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs."

We have mentioned about one hundred benefits of dhikr in our book *al-Wabil al-Sayyib wa Rafi' al-Kalim al-Tayyib* (The Heavy Rain and the Good Word that Ascends), and we mentioned there the secrets of dhikr, its great benefit and its excellent fruit. There we also mentioned that dhikr is of three kinds: the remembrance of the Names and Attributes and their meanings, praising Allah by them, and affirming the Oneness of Allah through them;

the remembrance of the command and prohibition, and of the lawful and the unlawful;

and the remembrance of Allah's favours, blessings and kindnesses.

It is also of three kinds: remembrance in which the heart and the tongue agree, which is the highest; remembrance by the heart alone, which is in the second rank; and remembrance by the bare tongue, which is in the third rank.

[Degrees of Dhikr]

[The First Degree: Outward Dhikr]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree is outward dhikr, which consists of praise, supplication or watchfulness.

By "outward" he means that which flows upon the tongue and corresponds to the heart, not mere tongue-movement, for the people of this path do not regard the latter as counting.

As for the remembrance of praise, it is like: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar. As for the remembrance of supplication, it is like: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers" (al-A'raf 7:23), and: "O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek help," and the like.

As for the remembrance of watchfulness, it is like the speaker's saying: "Allah is with me, Allah is watching me, Allah is my witness," and the like, which is used to strengthen presence with Allah. In it is the safeguarding of the good of the heart, the preservation of courtesy toward Allah, guarding against heedlessness, and seeking protection from Satan and the self.

The prophetic adhkar (remembrances) combine all three kinds, for they include praise of Allah, an opening for supplication and request, and an explicit statement of it, as in the hadith: "The best supplication is al-hamdu lillah." It was said to Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: "How did he make it a supplication?" He said: "Have you not heard the words of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt to Abd Allah ibn Jud'an, hoping for his gift:

*Shall I mention my need, or has your modesty sufficed me?*
*Your modesty is indeed your nature.*

*When a man praises you one day,*
*his praise suffices him from asking you.*"

So this is a created being who was content, from another created being, with praise of him instead of a request. How then is it with the Lord of the worlds?

The prophetic adhkar also include the fullness of watchfulness, the good of the heart, guarding against heedlessness, and seeking protection from distracting thoughts and Satan. And Allah knows best.

[Section: The Second Degree: Hidden Dhikr]

He said: The second degree is hidden dhikr, which is deliverance from fetters, remaining in witnessing (shuhud), and constant intimate conversation (musamara).

By "hidden" here he means remembrance by the heart alone, with whatever arises in it of inspirations (waridat), and this is the fruit of the first dhikr.

By "deliverance from fetters" he means being freed from heedlessness, forgetfulness and the veils that stand between the heart and the Lord, glorified is He. "Remaining in witnessing" means persisting in presence with the One remembered, and the heart witnessing Him until it is as if it sees Him.

"Constant intimate conversation" is the heart's ongoing private address to its Lord: sometimes in humble flattery, sometimes in lowly supplication, sometimes in praise, sometimes in glorification, and other kinds of secret and inward communion. This is the condition of every lover with his beloved, as it has been said:

*When we are alone, with the watcher present in the gathering,*
*we are silent, while desire speaks.*

[Section: The Third Degree: Real Dhikr]

He said: The third degree is real dhikr, which is witnessing the Real's remembrance of you, and being freed from witnessing your own remembrance, and recognising the pretence of the one who remembers in his remaining with the remembrance.

This remembrance in this degree is called "real" only because it is ascribed to the Lord, exalted is He. As for the ascription of remembrance to the servant, it is not real. Thus Allah's remembrance of His servant is the real remembrance, and it is witnessing that the Real remembers His servant, and remembers him among those whom He has singled out and qualified for nearness to Him and for His remembrance. So He made him one who remembers Him. In truth, He is the one who remembers Himself, by making His servant remember Him and by qualifying him for His remembrance. This meaning is what he alluded to in the chapter on Tawhid (Oneness) with his saying:

*His affirming of Himself is His affirming (of Oneness),*
*and the description of one who describes Him is a heretic's.*

That is, He is the one who in truth affirmed His own Oneness, so the servant's affirmation of Oneness is ascribed to Him in truth, and its ascription to the servant is not real.

For the servant, in that state, was neither by himself nor from himself; rather, he is placed in him. If he is called one who affirms Oneness and one who remembers, it is because he is the channel and locus of what flows in him, just as one is called white, black, tall or short because he is the locus of these attributes, having no making in them. His will did not bring them about, nor his power, nor his strength. This goes along with what accompanies it of being overwhelmed by nearness and by annihilation from the trace (rasm), and of absence through the witnessed from witnessing, and the strength of the inspiration. From this is composed a special taste: that no one affirmed Allah's Oneness except Allah, no one remembered Allah except Allah, and no one loved Allah except Allah.

This is the reality of what the people of this path hold. The knowers among them, the masters of insight, gave with this their due to servitude and their due to knowledge, and recognised that the servant is truly a servant in every respect, and the Lord is truly a Lord in every respect. They fulfilled the right of servitude through Allah, not through themselves, and for Allah, not for their own portions. They passed away in witnessing the meanings of His Names and Attributes from all else, and in what He loves and is pleased with, from what is accomplished by His will and decree. For the whole of existence is by Him, and what is His, namely His beloved and what pleases Him, is for Him and by Him. As for those who deviated, they passed away in what is by Him from what is for Him; so they took as allies His enemies, abandoned His religion, and equated His loves with His hatreds and the places of His pleasure with the places of His anger. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

His saying "recognising the pretence" means: by the annihilation of witnessing His remembrance of you from witnessing your remembrance of Him. This witnessing relieves the servant from seeing the self and from observing his own deeds, and it causes him to die and to live: it causes him to die to himself, and to live through his Lord; it annihilates him and separates him from himself and connects him to his Lord. This is the very attainment of victory over the self.

One of the knowers said: "The journey of the seekers ends in victory over their selves."

His saying "and recognising the pretence of the one who remembers in his remaining with the remembrance" means: the one who remains with the remembrance bears witness against himself that he is the one who remembers, and that is a pretence on his part, for he has no action of his own. This pretence does not leave him except when he passes away from his remembrance, for witnessing his own remembrance and remaining with it is a pretence that includes ascribing the remembrance to himself, while in truth it is not his.

It may be said: Glory be to Allah! What pretence is there in this? Is this not witnessing the realities as they are? For when he witnesses himself remembering, by Allah's making him one who remembers and His qualifying him for it, and by the remembrance of Allah coming before the servant's remembrance of Him, then both matters come together in his witnessing. So what pretence is there here? Is this not the very truth and the witnessing of realities as they are?

Yes, pretence is this: that he witnesses that remembrance as coming from himself, by his own power and strength, and not from Allah alone.

However, the Shaykh (the author of the source) is not restrained in annihilation by the blame of any blamer, nor does he listen to any reproacher in it.

What is beyond doubt is that remaining in dhikr is more perfect than annihilation in it and absence through it, because remaining contains detail, knowledge, witnessing realities as they are, and distinguishing between the Lord and the servant, between what subsists in the servant and what subsists in the Lord, exalted is He, and the witnessing of servanthood and the One served. Annihilation contains none of that. Annihilation, by its name, is annihilation, and subsistence is subsistence by its name. Annihilation is sought for something else, while subsistence is sought for its own sake. Annihilation is an attribute of the servant, and subsistence is an attribute of the Lord. Annihilation is non-existence, and subsistence is existence. Annihilation is negation, and subsistence is affirmation. Travelling on the path of annihilation is perilous, and how many deserts and ruins are in it! Travelling on the path of subsistence is safe, for the guides, the leaders and the protectors have trodden it. But the people of annihilation claim that it is a long road, yet they do not doubt its safety and its arrival at the goal. However, they claim that the path of annihilation is shorter, and that its rider flies, while the rider of the path of subsistence walks. The perfect among the travellers see annihilation as one station of the stations of the road, and its alighting is not general for every traveller; rather, some of them do not see it and do not pass by it. The greatest path and the most upright road is the path of subsistence. They argue against the one who is in annihilation by his moving from it to something else, for otherwise he is, in their view, in danger. And Allah is the One whose help is sought, and He, glorified is He, knows best.

(Section: Reading the Qur'an is better than dhikr, and dhikr is better than supplication)

This is considered by looking at each of them in isolation. However, what is less excellent may come to have a ruling that makes it preferable to the more excellent, indeed one that makes it obligatory, so that one may not turn away from it to the more excellent. Such is the glorification in bowing and prostration, for it is better than reciting the Qur'an in them; indeed, reciting in them is forbidden, whether as a prohibition or as a disapproval. Likewise, saying "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him) and "Rabbana wa lakal-hamd" (Our Lord, and to You be praise) in their places are better than recitation. Likewise the tashahhud. Likewise "Rabbi ighfir li, warhamni, wahdini, wa 'afini, warzuqni" (My Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide for me) between the two prostrations is better than recitation. Likewise the dhikr after the salam of the prayer, the remembrance of tahlil, tasbih, takbir and tahmid, is better than occupying oneself with recitation instead of it. Likewise, responding to the muezzin and saying as he says is better than recitation.

The excellence of the Qur'an over every other speech is like the excellence of God Most High over His creation. Yet every situation has its own fitting speech. Whenever the fitting speech is missed and one turns away from it to something else, wisdom is disturbed and the benefit intended from it is lost.

Likewise, beneficial remembrances (adhkar) suited to specific occasions are better than unrestricted recitation, and unrestricted recitation is better than unrestricted remembrances. The exception is when something befalls the servant that makes a remembrance or supplication more beneficial to him than reciting the Qur'an.

An example: he reflects on his sins, and this leads him to repentance through seeking forgiveness (istighfar), or something he fears harm from befalls him, from the devils of mankind and the jinn, so he turns to the remembrances and supplications that fortify and protect him.

Similarly, a servant may face a pressing need, and if he is occupied without asking for it, or with a remembrance in which his heart is not present, but when he turns to asking for it and calling upon God for it, his whole heart gathers upon God Most High and produces in him humility, submission, and earnest entreaty. In that state, his occupation with supplication is more beneficial, even though each of recitation and remembrance is more excellent and greater in reward.

This is a beneficial door that requires a discerning understanding (fiqh nafs) and a distinction (furqan) between the excellence of a thing in itself and its excellence that arises from circumstances. Thus one gives every possessor his right and places everything in its proper place: the eye has its place, the foot has its place, water has its place, and meat has its place.

Preserving the ranks (maratib) is part of the completeness of wisdom, which is the order of command and prohibition.

And God Most High is the Granter of success.

Likewise, soap and alkali (ashnan) are more beneficial for a garment at one time, while fumigation (tajmir), rosewater, and ironing it are more beneficial for it at another time.

One day I said to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may God have mercy on him: Some scholars were asked, "Which is more beneficial for the servant, glorification (tasbih) or seeking forgiveness (istighfar)?" He said: "If the garment is clean, then incense and rosewater are more beneficial for it; if it is soiled, then soap and hot water are more beneficial for it."

He said to me, may God have mercy on him: "How so, when the garments are still soiled?" Among this category is that the surah ﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas] equals one third of the Qur'an, yet with this it does not replace the verses on inheritance, divorce, khul' (divorce initiated by the wife), the waiting period ('iddah), and the like. Rather, those verses at their time and when needed are more beneficial than reciting the surah al-Ikhlas.

Since prayer comprises recitation, remembrance, and supplication, and gathers the components of servitude in the most complete way, it is more excellent than each of recitation, remembrance, and supplication alone, because it combines all of that together with the servitude of all the limbs.

This is a very beneficial principle that opens for the servant the door of knowing the ranks of deeds and placing them in their proper stations, so that he does not occupy himself with the lesser from the greater, thereby letting Iblis win the excess that lies between them, or look at the greater and occupy himself with it at the expense of the lesser when that is the time for the lesser, so that its benefit is entirely lost, supposing that his occupation with the greater yields more reward and greater recompense.

This requires knowledge of the ranks of deeds, their differences and purposes, and understanding in giving each deed its right and placing it in its rank, and in preferring what is more important over it, or forgoing what is superior and more excellent when it can be made up for and returned to. As for a lesser deed whose time, if missed, cannot be made up, then occupying oneself with it is preferable. An example of this is leaving recitation to return a greeting (radd al-salam) or to say "may God have mercy on you" to one who sneezes (tashmit al-atis), even though the Qur'an is more excellent, because he can occupy himself with this lesser act and then return to the greater; whereas if he occupies himself with recitation, he misses the benefit of returning the greeting and of saying "may God have mercy on you" to the sneezer. Likewise all deeds when they compete.

And God Most High is the Granter of success.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verses 41–43 (part 1 of 3):

Al-Jawhari said: *al-asil* (the late afternoon) is the time after the 'asr (afternoon) prayer until the maghrib (sunset). Its plural is *asl*, *aasal* and *asa'il*, as if it were *asila*.

The poet said:
"By my life, you are the house, honoring its people,
and I sit in its shade in the evenings."

It is also pluralized as *asjlan*, like *ba'ir* and *ba'ran* (camel and camels). Then they formed the diminutive of the plural, saying *asaylan*, then they replaced the final *n* with *l* and said *asaylal*.

The poet said:
"I stood there a while (*usaylalan*), asking it,
it could not answer, and there was no one in the abode."

**(Benefit)**

Among those who remember God are some who begin with the tongue, even while heedless, and then do not cease until the heart is present, so that the tongue and the heart agree in the remembrance. And among them are those who do not see this and do not begin in heedlessness, but remain still until the heart is present, and then begin the remembrance with the heart. When that grows strong, it draws the tongue along, and both agree together. The first one moves the remembrance from the tongue to the heart, and the second moves it from the heart to the tongue, without his heart ever being empty of it. Rather, he remains still at first until he senses the speaker manifesting within him. When he senses that, his heart speaks, then the inner speech passes into the outer remembrance of the tongue, and he then becomes immersed in it until he finds every part of himself remembering. The best and most beneficial remembrance is that in which the heart agrees with the tongue, that which is from the prophetic supplications, and in which the one remembering witnesses its meanings and purposes.

**[Chapter on the Station of Remembrance]**

Among the stations of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is the station of remembrance (*dhikr*). It is the great station of the people (the spiritual travelers), from which they take provisions, in which they trade, and to which they constantly return.

Remembrance is the banner of sovereignty (*wilaya*): whoever is given it is connected, and whoever is denied it is dismissed. It is the nourishment of the hearts of these people; when it leaves them, bodies become graves for them. It is the cultivation of their abodes, which, when left idle of it, become wasteland. It is their weapon, with which they fight the highway robbers, and their water, with which they extinguish the blazing of the path, and the cure for their ailments, when it departs from them, hearts relapse. It is the connecting cause and the bond that existed between them and the Knower of the unseen.

*"When we fall ill, we are treated by remembering you,*
*so we leave remembrance at times, and so we relapse."*

By it they ward off calamities, remove distresses, and by it hardships become easy for them. When trial overshadows them, to it is their refuge, and when calamities descend upon them, to it is their recourse. It is the gardens of their paradise in which they move about, and the capital of their happiness with which they trade. It leaves the sorrowful heart laughing and joyful, it brings the one who remembers to the One remembered, and indeed it leaves the one who remembers as one who is remembered.

In every limb there is a time-bound worship, but remembrance is the worship of the heart and the tongue, and it is not time-bound. Rather, they are commanded to remember their Worshipped and Beloved at all times: ﴿standing, sitting and on their sides﴾. Just as paradise is a barren plain and remembrance is its planting, so the hearts are wasteland and ruin, and remembrance is their cultivation and foundation.

It is the polish and burnish of hearts, and their medicine when illness overtakes them. Whenever the one who remembers increases in his remembrance, his immersion grows, and the One remembered becomes more beloved to him, and his longing for meeting Him increases. When his heart agrees with his tongue in remembrance, he forgets everything in the presence of that remembrance, God preserves everything for him, and it becomes a substitute for everything.

By it, deafness is removed from the ears, muteness from the tongues, and darkness is dispelled from the eyes. God adorns the tongues of those who remember with it, just as He adorns the sight of onlookers with light. So the heedless tongue is like a blind eye, a deaf ear and a paralyzed hand.

It is the greatest door of God, open between Him and His servant, so long as the servant does not close it through his heedlessness.

Al-Hasan al-Basri (may God have mercy on him) said: "Seek sweetness in three things: in the prayer, in remembrance, and in the recitation of the Qur'an. If you find it, well; if not, know that the door is closed."

Through remembrance, the servant overthrows Satan, just as Satan overthrows those who are heedless and forgetful.

One of the early generations (*salaf*) said: "When remembrance takes firm hold of the heart, if Satan approaches it, he is thrown down, just as a person is thrown down when Satan approaches him. Then the devils gather around him and say: 'What is wrong with this one?' It is said to them: 'The human has touched him.'"

It is the spirit of righteous deeds: when a deed is empty of remembrance, it is like a body without a spirit. And God knows best.

**[Chapter on the Aspects of Remembrance in the Qur'an]**

It appears in the Qur'an in ten aspects.

The first: the command to it, absolute and restricted.
The second: the prohibition of its opposite, heedlessness and forgetfulness.
The third: linking success (*falah*) to its continuity and abundance.
The fourth: praise of its people and the report of what God has prepared for them of paradise and forgiveness.
The fifth: the report of the loss of those who are diverted from it by other things.
The sixth: that He, glory be to Him, made His remembrance of them a reward for their remembrance of Him.
The seventh: the report that it is greater than everything.
The eighth: that He made it the seal of righteous deeds, just as it was their key.
The ninth: the report about its people that they are the ones who benefit from His signs, and that they alone are the people of understanding (*ulu al-albab*), to the exclusion of others.
The tenth: that He made it the companion of all righteous deeds and their spirit, so that when you lack it, they are like a body without a spirit.

**[Details of the Aspects of Remembrance in the Qur'an]**

A chapter on the explanation of these.

1. As for the first, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, remember God with frequent remembrance, and glorify Him morning and evening. It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out of darkness into light. And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41–43], and His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear﴾ [al-A'raf: 205].

On this there are two views: one, that it is in your secret self and heart; the other, that it is with your tongue, in such a way that you hear yourself.

2. As for the prohibition of its opposite, it is like His saying: ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾ [al-A'raf: 205], and His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot God, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾ [al-Hashr: 19].

3. As for linking success to its abundance, it is like His saying: ﴿And remember God much, that you may be successful﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

4. As for praise of its people and the goodness of their recompense, it is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women…﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35], up to His saying: ﴿and the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him much, God has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

5. As for the loss of those diverted from it, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that, they are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

6. As for His making His remembrance of them a reward for their remembrance of Him, it is like His saying: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152].

7. As for the report that it is greater than everything, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book, and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. And the remembrance of God is greater﴾ [al-Ankabut: 45]. On this there are four views:

One: that the remembrance of God is greater than everything, so it is the best of acts of worship, because the purpose of all acts of worship is to establish His remembrance; it is the secret and spirit of worship.

The second: the meaning is that when you remember Him, He remembers you, so His remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. According to this, the verbal noun (*masdar*) is attributed to the agent; according to the first, it is attributed to the object remembered.

The third: the meaning is that the remembrance of God is too great to let indecency and wrongdoing remain with it; rather, when the remembrance is complete, it erases every sin and disobedience. This is what the exegetes (*mufassirun*) have mentioned.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may God have mercy on him) say: The meaning of the verse is that prayer has two great benefits. One is that it prohibits indecency and wrongdoing. The second is that it includes the remembrance of God and contains Him and what it contains of the remembrance of God is greater than its prohibition of indecency and wrongdoing.

8. As for the sealing of righteous deeds with it: just as the act of fasting is sealed with His saying: ﴿and that you complete the period, and that you glorify God for having guided you, and that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185].

Hajj is sealed with it in His saying: ﴿So when you have completed your rites, remember God as you remember your fathers, or with even more remembrance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 200].

The prayer is sealed with it, as in His saying: ﴿So when you have completed the prayer, remember God standing, sitting and on your sides﴾ [al-Nisa': 103]. And the Friday prayer is sealed with it, as in His saying: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of God's bounty, and remember God much that you may be successful﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

For this reason, it is the seal of the worldly life, and if it is the last word of a servant, God admits him into paradise.

9. As for the restriction of those who remember to benefiting from His signs, and they are the people of understanding and intellect, it is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding, who remember God standing, sitting and on their sides﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190–191].

10. As for its companionship with all deeds, its being joined to them, and that it is their spirit: He, glory be to Him, joined it with the prayer, as in His saying: ﴿And establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ [Ta-Ha: 14]. He joined it with fasting and with Hajj and its rites; indeed, it is the spirit, core and purpose of Hajj. As the Prophet said: "The circling of the House, the running between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and the stoning of the pillars were only prescribed for the establishment of the remembrance of God."

He joined it with jihad, and commanded remembering Him when meeting opponents and confronting enemies, saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much, that you may be successful﴾ [al-Anfal: 45].

In a divine report, God says: "Indeed My servant, every one of My servants, who remembers Me while he is meeting his opponent…"

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may God sanctify his soul) cite it as evidence, and I heard him say: Lovers take pride in mentioning the one they love in this state, as 'Antarah said:

*"I remembered you while the spears were like*
*ropes of a well in the chest of a dark horse."*

Another said:

*"I remembered you while the spear swayed between us,*
*and the close-set dark spears had already drunk from us."*

Another said:

*"I remembered you while the spears were splintering,*
*holding, and the Indian swords dripped with my blood."*

This is abundant in their poetry, and it indicates the strength of love. For the lover's remembrance of his beloved in that state, when a man is concerned with nothing but himself, indicates that the beloved is for him in the position of his own self or dearer than it, and this is a proof of the sincerity of love. And God knows best.

**[Chapter on the Excellence of the People of Remembrance]**

Those who remember are the foremost, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of al-'Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of God was traveling on the road to Makkah when he passed a mountain called Jumdan, and said: 'Go on, this is Jumdan; the solitary ones (*al-mufarridun*) have outstripped.' They said: 'And who are the solitary ones, O Messenger of God?' He said: 'Those who remember God much, men and women.'" The *mufarridun* are either the monotheists (*al-muwahhidun*) or those who are alone and single.

In the Musnad, there is a raised (*marfu'*) hadith from Abu al-Darda' (may God be pleased with him): "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest in the sight of your King, the highest in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike yours?" They said: "And what is that, O Messenger of God?" He said: "The remembrance of God, mighty and majestic."

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Aghar say: "I testify concerning Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id (may God be pleased with them both) that they both bore witness concerning the Messenger of God that he said: 'No people sit remembering God except that the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and God mentions them among those who are with Him.'" This is in Sahih Muslim.

It suffices for the honor of remembrance that God boasts of its people to His angels, as in Sahih Muslim from Mu'awiyah (may God be pleased with him): "The Messenger of God went out to a circle of his companions and said: 'What has made you sit?' They said: 'We sat remembering God and praising Him for having guided us to Islam and bestowed it upon us.' He said: 'By God, did nothing but that make you sit?' They said: 'By God, nothing but that made us sit.' He said: 'As for me, I did not ask you to swear out of suspicion of you, but Jibril came to me and informed me that God boasts of you to the angels.'"

A Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deeds are the best?" He said: "That you depart this world while your tongue is still moist with the remembrance of Allah." A man said to him: "The laws of Islam have become too many for me, so instruct me in one thing that I may hold fast to." He said: "Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah."

In the Musnad and elsewhere, from the hadith of Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah came out to us and said: 'O people, graze in the gardens of Paradise!' We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the gardens of Paradise?' He said: 'The gatherings of dhikr.'"

He (ﷺ) also said: "Go out in the morning, return in the evening, and remember (Allah). Whoever wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him look at Allah's standing with him, for Allah lowers the servant to the place where He has lowered him in His own regard."

The Prophet (ﷺ) related from his father Ibrahim (peace be upon him), on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), that he said to him: "Convey my greetings of peace to your community and inform them that Paradise has pure soil and sweet water, that it is a level plain (qi'an), and that its planting is: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, Ahmad and others.

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ): "The likeness of one who remembers his Lord and one who does not remember Him is the likeness of the living and the dead." The wording of Muslim is: "The likeness of the house in which Allah is remembered and the house in which Allah is not remembered is the likeness of the living and the dead." Thus he made the house of the one who remembers like the house of the living, and the house of the heedless like the house of the dead, which is the grave.

In the first wording, he made the one who remembers like the living and the heedless like the dead. Both wordings thus imply that the heart that remembers is like one living among the dwellings of the living, and the heedless heart is like one dead among the dwellings of the dead. There is no doubt that the bodies of the heedless are graves for their hearts, and their hearts within them are like the dead in graves, as it has been said:

*Forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah is the death of their hearts,*
*and their bodies, before the graves, are graves.*

*And their spirits are in loneliness away from their bodies,*
*and for them there is no resurrection until the Resurrection.*

And as it has been said:

*Forgetfulness of the remembrance of Allah is the death of their hearts,*
*and their bodies are the effaced graves.*

*And their spirits are in loneliness away from their Beloved,*
*yet they are companions of the wicked.*

In a divine report: "Allah the Exalted says: 'When the remembrance of Me prevails over My servant, he loves Me and I love him.'"

In another: "'So rejoice in Me, and find delight in My remembrance.'"

In another: "'Son of Adam, you have not been fair to Me! I remember you while you forget Me; I call you while you flee to other than Me. I remove your afflictions while you are absorbed in your sins. Son of Adam, what will you say tomorrow when you come to Me?'"

In another: "'Son of Adam, remember Me when you are angry: I will remember you when I am angry. Be content with My help for you, for My help for you is better than your help for yourself.'"

In the Sahih, in the report that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrates from his Lord, blessed and exalted is He: "Whoever remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs."

We have mentioned about one hundred benefits of dhikr in our book *al-Wabil al-Sayyib wa Rafi' al-Kalim al-Tayyib* (The Heavy Rain and the Good Word that Ascends), and we mentioned there the secrets of dhikr, its great benefit and its excellent fruit. There we also mentioned that dhikr is of three kinds: the remembrance of the Names and Attributes and their meanings, praising Allah by them, and affirming the Oneness of Allah through them;

the remembrance of the command and prohibition, and of the lawful and the unlawful;

and the remembrance of Allah's favours, blessings and kindnesses.

It is also of three kinds: remembrance in which the heart and the tongue agree, which is the highest; remembrance by the heart alone, which is in the second rank; and remembrance by the bare tongue, which is in the third rank.

[Degrees of Dhikr]

[The First Degree: Outward Dhikr]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree is outward dhikr, which consists of praise, supplication or watchfulness.

By "outward" he means that which flows upon the tongue and corresponds to the heart, not mere tongue-movement, for the people of this path do not regard the latter as counting.

As for the remembrance of praise, it is like: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar. As for the remembrance of supplication, it is like: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers" (al-A'raf 7:23), and: "O Ever-Living, O Sustainer, by Your mercy I seek help," and the like.

As for the remembrance of watchfulness, it is like the speaker's saying: "Allah is with me, Allah is watching me, Allah is my witness," and the like, which is used to strengthen presence with Allah. In it is the safeguarding of the good of the heart, the preservation of courtesy toward Allah, guarding against heedlessness, and seeking protection from Satan and the self.

The prophetic adhkar (remembrances) combine all three kinds, for they include praise of Allah, an opening for supplication and request, and an explicit statement of it, as in the hadith: "The best supplication is al-hamdu lillah." It was said to Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: "How did he make it a supplication?" He said: "Have you not heard the words of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt to Abd Allah ibn Jud'an, hoping for his gift:

*Shall I mention my need, or has your modesty sufficed me?*
*Your modesty is indeed your nature.*

*When a man praises you one day,*
*his praise suffices him from asking you.*"

So this is a created being who was content, from another created being, with praise of him instead of a request. How then is it with the Lord of the worlds?

The prophetic adhkar also include the fullness of watchfulness, the good of the heart, guarding against heedlessness, and seeking protection from distracting thoughts and Satan. And Allah knows best.

[Section: The Second Degree: Hidden Dhikr]

He said: The second degree is hidden dhikr, which is deliverance from fetters, remaining in witnessing (shuhud), and constant intimate conversation (musamara).

By "hidden" here he means remembrance by the heart alone, with whatever arises in it of inspirations (waridat), and this is the fruit of the first dhikr.

By "deliverance from fetters" he means being freed from heedlessness, forgetfulness and the veils that stand between the heart and the Lord, glorified is He. "Remaining in witnessing" means persisting in presence with the One remembered, and the heart witnessing Him until it is as if it sees Him.

"Constant intimate conversation" is the heart's ongoing private address to its Lord: sometimes in humble flattery, sometimes in lowly supplication, sometimes in praise, sometimes in glorification, and other kinds of secret and inward communion. This is the condition of every lover with his beloved, as it has been said:

*When we are alone, with the watcher present in the gathering,*
*we are silent, while desire speaks.*

[Section: The Third Degree: Real Dhikr]

He said: The third degree is real dhikr, which is witnessing the Real's remembrance of you, and being freed from witnessing your own remembrance, and recognising the pretence of the one who remembers in his remaining with the remembrance.

This remembrance in this degree is called "real" only because it is ascribed to the Lord, exalted is He. As for the ascription of remembrance to the servant, it is not real. Thus Allah's remembrance of His servant is the real remembrance, and it is witnessing that the Real remembers His servant, and remembers him among those whom He has singled out and qualified for nearness to Him and for His remembrance. So He made him one who remembers Him. In truth, He is the one who remembers Himself, by making His servant remember Him and by qualifying him for His remembrance. This meaning is what he alluded to in the chapter on Tawhid (Oneness) with his saying:

*His affirming of Himself is His affirming (of Oneness),*
*and the description of one who describes Him is a heretic's.*

That is, He is the one who in truth affirmed His own Oneness, so the servant's affirmation of Oneness is ascribed to Him in truth, and its ascription to the servant is not real.

For the servant, in that state, was neither by himself nor from himself; rather, he is placed in him. If he is called one who affirms Oneness and one who remembers, it is because he is the channel and locus of what flows in him, just as one is called white, black, tall or short because he is the locus of these attributes, having no making in them. His will did not bring them about, nor his power, nor his strength. This goes along with what accompanies it of being overwhelmed by nearness and by annihilation from the trace (rasm), and of absence through the witnessed from witnessing, and the strength of the inspiration. From this is composed a special taste: that no one affirmed Allah's Oneness except Allah, no one remembered Allah except Allah, and no one loved Allah except Allah.

This is the reality of what the people of this path hold. The knowers among them, the masters of insight, gave with this their due to servitude and their due to knowledge, and recognised that the servant is truly a servant in every respect, and the Lord is truly a Lord in every respect. They fulfilled the right of servitude through Allah, not through themselves, and for Allah, not for their own portions. They passed away in witnessing the meanings of His Names and Attributes from all else, and in what He loves and is pleased with, from what is accomplished by His will and decree. For the whole of existence is by Him, and what is His, namely His beloved and what pleases Him, is for Him and by Him. As for those who deviated, they passed away in what is by Him from what is for Him; so they took as allies His enemies, abandoned His religion, and equated His loves with His hatreds and the places of His pleasure with the places of His anger. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

His saying "recognising the pretence" means: by the annihilation of witnessing His remembrance of you from witnessing your remembrance of Him. This witnessing relieves the servant from seeing the self and from observing his own deeds, and it causes him to die and to live: it causes him to die to himself, and to live through his Lord; it annihilates him and separates him from himself and connects him to his Lord. This is the very attainment of victory over the self.

One of the knowers said: "The journey of the seekers ends in victory over their selves."

His saying "and recognising the pretence of the one who remembers in his remaining with the remembrance" means: the one who remains with the remembrance bears witness against himself that he is the one who remembers, and that is a pretence on his part, for he has no action of his own. This pretence does not leave him except when he passes away from his remembrance, for witnessing his own remembrance and remaining with it is a pretence that includes ascribing the remembrance to himself, while in truth it is not his.

It may be said: Glory be to Allah! What pretence is there in this? Is this not witnessing the realities as they are? For when he witnesses himself remembering, by Allah's making him one who remembers and His qualifying him for it, and by the remembrance of Allah coming before the servant's remembrance of Him, then both matters come together in his witnessing. So what pretence is there here? Is this not the very truth and the witnessing of realities as they are?

Yes, pretence is this: that he witnesses that remembrance as coming from himself, by his own power and strength, and not from Allah alone.

However, the Shaykh (the author of the source) is not restrained in annihilation by the blame of any blamer, nor does he listen to any reproacher in it.

What is beyond doubt is that remaining in dhikr is more perfect than annihilation in it and absence through it, because remaining contains detail, knowledge, witnessing realities as they are, and distinguishing between the Lord and the servant, between what subsists in the servant and what subsists in the Lord, exalted is He, and the witnessing of servanthood and the One served. Annihilation contains none of that. Annihilation, by its name, is annihilation, and subsistence is subsistence by its name. Annihilation is sought for something else, while subsistence is sought for its own sake. Annihilation is an attribute of the servant, and subsistence is an attribute of the Lord. Annihilation is non-existence, and subsistence is existence. Annihilation is negation, and subsistence is affirmation. Travelling on the path of annihilation is perilous, and how many deserts and ruins are in it! Travelling on the path of subsistence is safe, for the guides, the leaders and the protectors have trodden it. But the people of annihilation claim that it is a long road, yet they do not doubt its safety and its arrival at the goal. However, they claim that the path of annihilation is shorter, and that its rider flies, while the rider of the path of subsistence walks. The perfect among the travellers see annihilation as one station of the stations of the road, and its alighting is not general for every traveller; rather, some of them do not see it and do not pass by it. The greatest path and the most upright road is the path of subsistence. They argue against the one who is in annihilation by his moving from it to something else, for otherwise he is, in their view, in danger. And Allah is the One whose help is sought, and He, glorified is He, knows best.

(Section: Reading the Qur'an is better than dhikr, and dhikr is better than supplication)

This is considered by looking at each of them in isolation. However, what is less excellent may come to have a ruling that makes it preferable to the more excellent, indeed one that makes it obligatory, so that one may not turn away from it to the more excellent. Such is the glorification in bowing and prostration, for it is better than reciting the Qur'an in them; indeed, reciting in them is forbidden, whether as a prohibition or as a disapproval. Likewise, saying "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him) and "Rabbana wa lakal-hamd" (Our Lord, and to You be praise) in their places are better than recitation. Likewise the tashahhud. Likewise "Rabbi ighfir li, warhamni, wahdini, wa 'afini, warzuqni" (My Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, guide me, grant me well-being, and provide for me) between the two prostrations is better than recitation. Likewise the dhikr after the salam of the prayer, the remembrance of tahlil, tasbih, takbir and tahmid, is better than occupying oneself with recitation instead of it. Likewise, responding to the muezzin and saying as he says is better than recitation.

The excellence of the Qur'an over every other speech is like the excellence of God Most High over His creation. Yet every situation has its own fitting speech. Whenever the fitting speech is missed and one turns away from it to something else, wisdom is disturbed and the benefit intended from it is lost.

Likewise, beneficial remembrances (adhkar) suited to specific occasions are better than unrestricted recitation, and unrestricted recitation is better than unrestricted remembrances. The exception is when something befalls the servant that makes a remembrance or supplication more beneficial to him than reciting the Qur'an.

An example: he reflects on his sins, and this leads him to repentance through seeking forgiveness (istighfar), or something he fears harm from befalls him, from the devils of mankind and the jinn, so he turns to the remembrances and supplications that fortify and protect him.

Similarly, a servant may face a pressing need, and if he is occupied without asking for it, or with a remembrance in which his heart is not present, but when he turns to asking for it and calling upon God for it, his whole heart gathers upon God Most High and produces in him humility, submission, and earnest entreaty. In that state, his occupation with supplication is more beneficial, even though each of recitation and remembrance is more excellent and greater in reward.

This is a beneficial door that requires a discerning understanding (fiqh nafs) and a distinction (furqan) between the excellence of a thing in itself and its excellence that arises from circumstances. Thus one gives every possessor his right and places everything in its proper place: the eye has its place, the foot has its place, water has its place, and meat has its place.

Preserving the ranks (maratib) is part of the completeness of wisdom, which is the order of command and prohibition.

And God Most High is the Granter of success.

Likewise, soap and alkali (ashnan) are more beneficial for a garment at one time, while fumigation (tajmir), rosewater, and ironing it are more beneficial for it at another time.

One day I said to Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may God have mercy on him: Some scholars were asked, "Which is more beneficial for the servant, glorification (tasbih) or seeking forgiveness (istighfar)?" He said: "If the garment is clean, then incense and rosewater are more beneficial for it; if it is soiled, then soap and hot water are more beneficial for it."

He said to me, may God have mercy on him: "How so, when the garments are still soiled?" Among this category is that the surah ﴿Say: He is God, the One﴾ [al-Ikhlas] equals one third of the Qur'an, yet with this it does not replace the verses on inheritance, divorce, khul' (divorce initiated by the wife), the waiting period ('iddah), and the like. Rather, those verses at their time and when needed are more beneficial than reciting the surah al-Ikhlas.

Since prayer comprises recitation, remembrance, and supplication, and gathers the components of servitude in the most complete way, it is more excellent than each of recitation, remembrance, and supplication alone, because it combines all of that together with the servitude of all the limbs.

This is a very beneficial principle that opens for the servant the door of knowing the ranks of deeds and placing them in their proper stations, so that he does not occupy himself with the lesser from the greater, thereby letting Iblis win the excess that lies between them, or look at the greater and occupy himself with it at the expense of the lesser when that is the time for the lesser, so that its benefit is entirely lost, supposing that his occupation with the greater yields more reward and greater recompense.

This requires knowledge of the ranks of deeds, their differences and purposes, and understanding in giving each deed its right and placing it in its rank, and in preferring what is more important over it, or forgoing what is superior and more excellent when it can be made up for and returned to. As for a lesser deed whose time, if missed, cannot be made up, then occupying oneself with it is preferable. An example of this is leaving recitation to return a greeting (radd al-salam) or to say "may God have mercy on you" to one who sneezes (tashmit al-atis), even though the Qur'an is more excellent, because he can occupy himself with this lesser act and then return to the greater; whereas if he occupies himself with recitation, he misses the benefit of returning the greeting and of saying "may God have mercy on you" to the sneezer. Likewise all deeds when they compete.

And God Most High is the Granter of success.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verse 44:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be "Peace."﴾ This is their greeting on the day they meet Him, may He be blessed and exalted. It is impossible that this be a greeting from them to Him, for they know Him too well to greet Him with peace, and they were forbidden from that in this world. Rather, this is a greeting from Him to them.

So that is a greeting to them at the time of meeting, just as the beloved greets his beloved when he meets him. What, then, will those veiled from their Lord lose on that day?!

؎ Let it suffice that the one who is absent from you is absent; that is a sin whose punishment lies within it.

(Benefit)

The scholars of the Arabic language (ahl al-lugha) agreed that meeting (al-liqa') here can only mean direct witnessing and seeing with the eyes. And that such an isnad is sufficient for you in its soundness. Meeting is established by the explicit text of the Qur'an as has preceded, and by mass transmission (tawatur) from the Prophet (ﷺ). And all the hadiths about meeting are sound, such as the hadith of Anas in the account of the incident of Bi'r Ma'una:

"We have met our Lord, and He is pleased with us and has made us pleased."

And the hadith of 'Ubada, 'A'isha, Abu Hurayra and Ibn Mas'ud:

"Whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him."

And the hadith of Anas:

"You will face, after me, favoritism, so be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger."

And the hadith of Abu Dharr: "If you come to Me with earth-full of sins, then meet Me not associating anything with Me, I will come to you with earth-full of forgiveness."

And the hadith of Abu Musa:

"Whoever meets Allah not associating anything with Him enters Paradise."

And other hadiths about meeting, all of which are consistent in one wording.

(Section)

Concerning the threat against those who deny the vision (ru'ya). The words of the Most High have preceded: ﴿Nay, indeed they will be veiled from their Lord that Day.﴾

And the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak: "Allah does not veil anyone from Him except that He punishes him," then he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿Then indeed they will burn in the Hellfire. Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny."﴾

He said this concerning the vision.

Muslim recorded in his Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, who said: They said, "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the sun at noon when there are no clouds?" They said: "No." He said: "Do you have any difficulty seeing the moon on the night of the full moon when there are no clouds?" They said: "No." He said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will not have any difficulty seeing your Lord, except as you have difficulty seeing one of them. He will meet the servant and say: 'O so-and-so, did I not honor you, make you chief, marry you, subject to you horses and camels, and leave you to lead and to enjoy a quarter (of the spoils)?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'Did you think that you would meet Me?' He will say: 'No.' He will say: 'Then I forget you as you forgot Me.' Then he will meet the second and say the same: 'O so-and-so, did I not honor you...' He will say: 'Yes, O Lord.' He will say: 'Did you think that you would meet Me?' He will say: 'No.' He will say: 'Then I forget you as you forgot Me.' Then he will meet the third and say the same to him, and he will say: 'O Lord, I believed in You, in Your Book, and in Your Messengers, I prayed, I fasted, and I gave charity,' and he will praise himself as much as he can. He will say: 'Here, then.' Then it will be said to him: 'Now We will send Our witness against you,' and he will reflect within himself: 'Who is it that will testify against me?' His mouth will be sealed, and his thigh, his flesh and his bones will be told: 'Speak!' So his thigh, his flesh and his bones will speak of his deeds. This is so that he has no excuse from himself, and that is the hypocrite, and that is the one with whom Allah is displeased."

So combine His saying "Indeed you will see your Lord" with His saying "for whoever thought he would not meet Him, I forget him as you forgot Me."

And the consensus of the scholars of the language that meeting means direct seeing with the eyes will give you the knowledge that the denier of the vision is more deserving of this threat. Among the chapter headings of the People of the Sunna on this hadith is "A chapter on the threat against those who deny the vision," as the Shaykh al-Islam and others did. And success is from Allah.

God Most High named him "a lamp giving light" (sirajan muniran), and named the sun "a blazing lamp" (sirajan wahhajan). People's need for the giving-light lamp is greater than their need for the blazing lamp, for the blazing lamp is needed at some times and not others, whereas the giving-light lamp is needed at every time, in every place, by night and by day, in private and in public.

And he said in (Zad al-Ma'ad):

Al-Munir is the one that gives light without burning, unlike al-Wahhaj, for in it there is a kind of burning and blazing.

God Most High named him "a lamp giving light" (sirajan muniran), and named the sun "a blazing lamp" (sirajan wahhajan). People's need for the giving-light lamp is greater than their need for the blazing lamp, for the blazing lamp is needed at some times and not others, whereas the giving-light lamp is needed at every time, in every place, by night and by day, in private and in public.

And he said in (Zad al-Ma'ad):

Al-Munir is the one that gives light without burning, unlike al-Wahhaj, for in it there is a kind of burning and blazing.

[The Ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that Divorce Lies in the Hand of the Husband and Not in the Hand of Anyone Else]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them…﴾

And He says: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term, then either retain them in a good manner or release them in a good manner﴾ [al-Baqarah: 231].

So He made divorce belong to the one who contracted the marriage, because he holds the power of retention (imsak), which is the return (raj'ah).

Ibn Majah narrated in his Sunan, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! My master married me to his slave-woman, and he wants to separate me from her.'

So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit and said: 'O people, what is the matter with one of you who marries his slave to his slave-woman and then wants to separate them? Divorce belongs only to the one who holds the leg (bi-al-saq).'"

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', from (Ibn 'Abbas – may Allah be pleased with them both – who used to say: "The divorce of a slave is in the hand of his master. If he divorces, it is valid, and if he separates them, it is one divorce, when both of them belong to him. But if the slave belongs to him and the slave-woman belongs to someone else, the master of the slave-woman may also divorce, if he wishes.")

Al-Thawri narrated from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from ('Ata', from him: "The divorce of a slave, or his separation, is nothing.")

'Abd al-Razzaq mentioned: Ibn Jurayj related to us, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard (Jabir say concerning the slave-woman and the slave: "Their master unites them and separates them.")

The judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is more worthy of being followed, and the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas – may Allah be pleased with them both – mentioned earlier, although there is what there is in its chain, is supported by the Qur'an, and the practice of the people is in accordance with it.
