For his (ﷺ) saying "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad" is a imperative (requesting) sentence, while his saying "as You sent blessings upon the family of Ibrahim" is a declarative sentence. When an imperative sentence occurs in the place of supplication and request, expanding and lengthening it is more fitting than shortening and omitting it. For this reason it is prescribed to repeat it, to begin it, and to restate it, for it is supplication, and Allah loves those who insist in supplication. For this reason you will find that many of the supplications of the Prophet (ﷺ) contain an expansion of expressions and the mention of every meaning in its explicit wording, without relying on the indication of another wording. What attests to this is his (ﷺ) saying in the hadith of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), which Muslim narrated in his Sahih: "O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have done later, what I have done secretly and what I have done openly, what I have exceeded in, and what You know better than I. You are the One who brings forward and You are the One who puts back; there is no god but You." And it is known that if it were said "forgive me all that I have done," it would be more concise; but the wording of the hadith, in a context of supplication, humility, manifesting servitude and neediness, and calling to mind the kinds of sins from which the servant repents in detail, is better and more eloquent than brevity and abbreviation.

Likewise is his saying in another hadith: "O Allah, forgive me all my sin, its small and its great, its secret and its open, its first and its last."

And in another hadith: "O Allah, forgive me my wrongdoing, my ignorance, my excess in my affair, and what You know better than I. O Allah, forgive me my seriousness and my jest, my errors and my deliberate faults, and all of that is with me."

This is abundant in the transmitted supplications, for supplication is servitude to Allah the Exalted, neediness toward Him, and humility before Him. Therefore, the more the servant multiplies it, lengthens it, repeats it, begins it, and varies its phrases, the more eloquent it is in his servitude, in manifesting his poverty, humility and need, and it is closer for him to his Lord and greater for his reward. This is unlike the created being, for the more you ask him and repeat your needs to him, the more you weary him, burden him and lower yourself in his eyes; and the more you leave off asking him, the greater you are in his sight and the more beloved to him. But Allah, glorified and exalted, the more you ask Him, the nearer and more beloved you are to Him; and the more you persist in supplicating to Him, the more He loves you, and whoever does not ask Him, He is angry with him.

(Allah is angered if you leave off asking Him, / and the son of Adam is angered when he is asked.)

So the object sought increases with the increase of request and decreases with its decrease.

As for the declarative report, it is a report of a matter that has occurred and ended, which does not admit of increase or decrease; so there is no great benefit in increasing the wording in it, especially since the context is not one of clarifying and making the addressee understand, such that expansion and elaboration would be fitting. So brevity and abbreviation in it are more complete and better. For this reason it came with the word Ibrahim at one time and with the word "his family" at another, because each of the two words indicates what the other indicates, in the aspect we have already mentioned. Thus the intended meaning of the two wordings is one, with brevity and abbreviation. But in request, if it were said "send blessings upon Muhammad," there would be nothing in this to indicate blessing upon his family, since it is a request and supplication formed with this wording, not a report of a matter that has occurred and been established. And if it were said "send blessings upon the family of Muhammad," the Prophet (ﷺ) would be blessed only in generality; so it is said "upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad," for he thereby receives the blessing upon him specifically and the blessing upon him by his inclusion in his family.

Here people have two approaches to such a case:

One is to say that he is included in his family while being mentioned by name, so he is mentioned twice: once specifically and once in the general wording. On this view, he has been blessed twice: specifically and generally. This is based on the principle of those who say that when the general is mentioned after the specific, it also encompasses it. And the specific is mentioned twice: once specifically and once by its inclusion in the general wording. Likewise is the mention of the specific after the general, such as the saying of the Exalted: "Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael, then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers" [Al-Baqarah: 98].

And like the saying of the Exalted: "And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Noah, and Abraham" [Al-Ahzab: 7].

The second approach: mentioning him by the specific wording indicates that he is not included in the general wording; so mentioning him specifically suffices from his inclusion in the general wording. On this approach there are benefits in that:

Among them: since he is among the most noble of the general category, he is singled out by a wording that specifically indicates him, as if he were separated from the category and distinguished from them by what requires that he be distinguished by a wording specific to him. This is therefore an indication of his particularity and his excellence over the category included in the general wording.

The second: that it contains an indication that the blessing upon him is the origin, and the blessing upon his family is a follower of him, which they attained only by following him.

The third: that singling him out by mention removes the suspicion of specification, and that it is not permissible for him to be excluded from the general wording; rather he is intended with certainty.

(Section: On the occasions of blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ) for which sending blessings is especially emphasized, whether obligatory or strongly recommended.)

The first occasion, which is the most important and most emphasized, is in the prayer at the end of the tashahhud. The Muslims have agreed upon its legislation, but they differed as to whether it is obligatory within it. One group said it is not obligatory in it, and they ascribed those who held it obligatory to deviation and opposition to consensus, among them al-Tahawi, al-Qadi Iyad and al-Khattabi; for he said: "It is not obligatory in prayer," and this is the view of the majority of jurists except al-Shafi'i, and I know of no precedent for it. Likewise Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned that al-Shafi'i stood alone in this and chose the non-obligatory view.

Others disputed with them, both in transmission and in argument, and said:

As for your ascribing al-Shafi'i and those who held his view in this question to deviation and opposition to consensus, it is not correct, for a group of the Companions and those after them held his view.

Among them is Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, for he regarded it as obligatory in prayer and would say: "There is no prayer for one who does not send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in it." Ibn Abd al-Barr reported this from him in al-Tamhid, and others also related it.

(The second occasion of blessing upon him (ﷺ): in the first tashahhud.)

This has been differed upon. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-Umm that one sends blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in the first tashahhud; this is the well-known view of his school, and it is the newer opinion, but it is recommended and not obligatory.

He said in the older opinion: one does not add to the tashahhud. This is the narration of al-Muzani from him. Ahmad, Abu Hanifa, Malik and others said likewise.

(The third occasion of blessing upon him (ﷺ): blessing upon him at the end of the qunut.)

Al-Shafi'i and those who agree with him recommended it.

(The fourth occasion of blessing upon him (ﷺ): the funeral prayer, after the second takbir.)

There is no disagreement about its legislation within it. But there is disagreement about whether the validity of the funeral prayer depends on it. Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, in the well-known view of their school, said it is obligatory within the prayer and the prayer is not valid without it; and al-Bayhaqi narrated this from Ubada ibn al-Samit and other Companions.

Malik and Abu Hanifa said it is recommended and not obligatory, and this is one view of al-Shafi'i's followers.

(The fifth occasion of blessing upon him (ﷺ): in the sermon.)

There is disagreement about whether it is a condition for the validity of the sermon.

Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, in the well-known view of their school, said the sermon is not valid except with blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ).

Abu Hanifa and Malik said it is valid without it, and this is a view in Ahmad's school.

(The sixth occasion of blessing upon him (ﷺ): blessing upon him after answering the muezzin and at the iqamah.)

Because Muslim narrated in his Sahih from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When you hear the muezzin, say the same as he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends blessings upon me, Allah sends blessings upon him tenfold. Then ask Allah for al-Wasilah for me, for it is a station in Paradise, not fitting except for one of the servants of Allah, and I hope that I will be he. So whoever asks Allah for al-Wasilah for me, intercession becomes due to him."

Al-Hasan ibn Arafa said: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti narrated to me, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, who said: "Whoever says the same as the muezzin says, and when the muezzin says 'the prayer has been established,' he says: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, and bring him to the rank of al-Wasilah in Paradise,' he has entered into the intercession of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Yusuf ibn Asbat said: It has reached me that when the prayer is established and a man does not say: "O Allah, Lord of this answered call, the call that is answered, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and marry us to the dark-eyed houris," the houris say: "How little you desire us!"

In answering the muezzin there are five sunnahs from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr includes three of them.

The fourth is that one says what al-Muslim narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever says, when he hears the muezzin: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger; I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Muhammad as Messenger, and with Islam as religion,' his sins will be forgiven."

The fifth is that one supplicates to Allah after answering the muezzin, and blesses His Messenger (ﷺ), and asks Him for al-Wasilah, because in Sunan Abi Dawud and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Amr, a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, the muezzins are surpassing us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say as they say, and when you finish, ask, and you will be given." [Its chain is sound.]

In the Musnad, from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when the caller calls: 'O Allah, Lord of this established call and beneficial prayer, send blessings upon Muhammad and be pleased with me with a pleasure after which there is no anger,' Allah answers his supplication."

In al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim, from the hadith of Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he heard the muezzin, would say: "O Allah, Lord of this call, the call that is answered, the word of truth and the word of piety; cause us to die upon it, cause us to live upon it, and make us among its righteous people, alive and dead."

These are twenty-five sunnahs in the day and night, which none but the foremost hold to.

(The seventh occasion of blessing upon him (ﷺ): during supplication.)

It has three levels.

The first: that one sends blessings upon him before the supplication and after praising Allah the Exalted.

The second level: that one sends blessings upon him at the beginning, middle and end of the supplication.

The third: that one sends blessings upon him at its beginning and end, and places one's need between them.

(The eighth occasion of blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ): upon entering the mosque and upon leaving it.)

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verse 56 (part 6 of 9):

Ibn Khuzaymah in his Sahih and Abu Hatim ibn Hibban related from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: 'O Allah, open for me the gates of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: 'O Allah, protect me from the accursed Shaytan.'"

(The ninth occasion for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): at al-Safa and al-Marwah)

Isma'il ibn Ishaq related in his book: Hudbah narrated to us, Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, Nafi' narrated to us from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to glorify Allah at al-Safa three times, saying: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion, to Him belongs all praise, and He is powerful over all things." Then he would send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then supplicate, prolonging the standing and the supplication. Then he would do the same at al-Marwah. This is also among the accompaniments of supplication. [Its chain is sahih.]

(The tenth occasion: when people gather before they disperse)

The hadiths on this have already been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) by more than one route, that he said: "No group sits in a gathering, then disperses without having mentioned Allah and without having sent blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), except that it will be a deficiency (tirah) for them from Allah. If He wills, He will punish them, and if He wills, He will forgive them." Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Hakim and others related it.

Abd Allah ibn Idris al-Awdi related from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, from Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) who said: "Adorn your gatherings with sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ)." [A mawquf sahih report, i.e., one stopped at a Companion.]

It is also mentioned from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him).

(The eleventh occasion: upon mention of him (ﷺ))

Scholars differed on whether it is obligatory to send blessings upon him (ﷺ) each time his name is mentioned. Abu Ja'far al-Tahawi and Abu Abd Allah al-Halimi said: it is obligatory to send blessings upon him (ﷺ) each time his name is mentioned.

Others said that this is recommended (mustahabb) and not an obligation whose neglect is sinful. Then they differed. One group said it is obligatory once in a lifetime, because a command in absolute form does not require repetition, and the reality (of the act) is achieved by one instance. This is reported from Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Thawri and al-Awza'i.

Iyad and Ibn Abd al-Barr said: this is the view of the majority of the community.

Another group said: rather, it is obligatory in every prayer in which one sits for the final tashahhud, as mentioned before. This is the view of al-Shafi'i and of Ahmad in the last of his two reported positions, and others.

A group said: the command to send blessings is a command of recommendation, not of obligation. This is the view of Ibn Jarir and a group, and Ibn Jarir claimed consensus (ijma') regarding it. This is consistent with his principle, for when he saw the majority on one view he considered it a consensus that must be followed. The two premises here are false.

(The twelfth occasion: upon completing the talbiyah)

Al-Daraqutni said: Muhammad ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Ali ibn Zakariyya al-Tammar narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Humayd narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah al-Umawi narrated to us, who said: I heard Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Za'idah narrate from Umarah ibn Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) when he finished his talbiyah would ask Allah, Exalted is He, for His forgiveness and His pleasure, and seek refuge in His mercy from the Fire. Salih said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: it was recommended for a man, when he finished his talbiyah, to send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ).

(The thirteenth occasion: upon touching the Black Stone (al-Hajar al-Aswad))

Abu Dhar al-Harawi said: Muhammad ibn Bukran informed us, Abu Abd Allah ibn Makhlad informed us, Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Awn ibn Sallam informed us, Muhammad ibn Sallam narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Muhajir narrated to us from Nafi', who said: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), when he wished to touch the Black Stone, would say: "O Allah, (I do this) in faith in You, in belief in Your Book, and in the Sunnah of Your Prophet (ﷺ)," and then he would touch it. It has already been mentioned that among the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) is at al-Safa and al-Marwah.

(The fourteenth occasion: upon standing at his grave (ﷺ))

Sahnun said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to us from Malik, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, who said: I saw Abd Allah ibn Umar stand at the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ), send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and supplicate for Abu Bakr and Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both). Malik mentioned it in al-Muwatta.

Malik also said, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Abd Allah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that when he intended a journey or returned from a journey, he would come to the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ), send blessings upon him and supplicate, then depart. Ibn Numayr said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Abd Allah narrated to us from Nafi', from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that when he returned from a journey he would begin with the grave of the Prophet (ﷺ), send blessings upon him without touching the grave, then greet Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), then say: "Peace be upon you, O father."

(The fifteenth occasion: when one goes out to the market, to a banquet, or the like)

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Mis'ar narrated to us, Amir ibn Shaqiq narrated to us from Abu Wa'il, who said: I never saw Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud) sit at a banquet, at a funeral, or at anything else, but that he would stand up after praising Allah and extolling Him, sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and supplicating with various supplications. If he went out to the market, he would come to the most remote spot and sit there, praising Allah, sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and supplicating with various supplications.

(The sixteenth occasion: when a man rises from the night sleep)

Al-Nasa'i in his Sunan al-Kubra said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali informed us, Khalaf, that is Ibn Tamim, narrated to us, Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, Shurayk narrated to us from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, laughs at two men: a man who met the enemy, being on a horse of the best of his companions' horses, when they fled, while he stood firm; if he is killed, he is a martyr, and if he survives, he is the one at whom Allah laughs. And a man who stood up in the depth of the night, when no one knew of him, performed ablution and perfected it, then praised Allah and glorified Him, sent blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and began the recitation of the Qur'an. He is the one at whom Allah laughs, saying: "Look at My servant standing, whom no one sees but Me."

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar narrated to us from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "Two men at whom Allah laughs..." and he mentioned it in a similar manner.

(The seventeenth occasion: after completing the recitation of the Qur'an)

This is because the place is a place of supplication. Imam Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) explicitly stated the supplication after completing the Qur'an. In the narration of Abu al-Harith he said: "When Anas completed the Qur'an, he would gather his family and children."

In the narration of Yusuf ibn Musa, when he was asked about a man who completes the Qur'an and people gather around him to supplicate, he said: "Yes. I saw Ma'mar do it when he completed it."

In the narration of Harb he said: "I recommend that when a man completes the Qur'an he gather his family and supplicate."

Ibn Abi Dawud, in Fada'il al-Qur'an, related from al-Hakam who said: Mujahid sent for me, and Ibn Abi Lababah was with him, saying: "We have sent for you, for we intend to complete the Qur'an." It was said that supplication is answered at the completion of the Qur'an, and then they supplicated with various supplications.

He also related in that book from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Whoever completes the Qur'an has an answered supplication."

And from Mujahid who said: "Mercy descends at the completion of the Qur'an."

Abu Ubayd in his book Fada'il al-Qur'an related from Qatadah who said: In Madinah there was a man who recited the Qur'an from beginning to end to his companions. Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) would post watchers, and when it came to the completion, Ibn Abbas would come and attend it.

Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) explicitly stated the recommendation of this in the tarawih prayer. Hanbal said: "I heard Ahmad say, regarding the completion of the Qur'an: when you finish your recitation with 'Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind' (﴿Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾), raise your hands in supplication before bowing." I said: "What do you base this on?" He said: "I saw the people of Makkah doing it, and Sufyan ibn Uyaynah used to do it with them in Makkah."

Abbas ibn Abd al-Azim said: "And thus I found people in Basrah and Makkah (doing it)." The people of Madinah narrate many things on this, and he mentioned it from Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him).

Al-Fadl ibn Ziyad said: "I asked Abu Abd Allah: Should I complete the Qur'an in the tarawih or in the witr?" He said: "Do it in the tarawih, so that there is a supplication for us between the two (rak'ahs)." I said: "How should I do it?" He said: "When you finish the last of the Qur'an, raise your hands before you bow, and supplicate for us while we are in the prayer, and prolong the standing." I said: "What should I supplicate with?" He said: "With whatever you wish." Al-Fadl said: "So I did as he commanded me, while he was behind me supplicating, standing and raising his hands."

Since this is among the most emphatic occasions for supplication and most deserving of being answered, it is also among the most emphatic occasions for sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ).

(The eighteenth occasion: on Friday)

There has already been mentioned in this regard the hadith of Aws ibn Aws, from Abu Umamah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Send abundant blessings upon me every Friday, for the prayer of my community is presented to me every Friday. Whoever is most abundant in sending blessings upon me will be nearest to me in rank." (ﷺ). Al-Bayhaqi related it, and it has already been mentioned.

It is also related from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday, for no one sends blessings upon me on Friday except that his blessing is presented to me." In its chain is Isma'il ibn Rafi'. Ya'qub ibn Sufyan said: "His hadith is suitable for corroboration and supporting narrations."

Ibn Adi said: Isma'il ibn Musa al-Hasib narrated to us, Jabbarah ibn Mughallis narrated to us, Abu Ishaq al-Khumaysi narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday, for your blessings are presented to me." Although its chain is weak, it is preserved in general terms, and its mention among supporting reports is not harmful.

It has already been mentioned in the mursal reports of al-Hasan from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday."

Ibn Wadhdhah said: Abu Marwan al-Bazzar narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us from Ibn Shu'ayb, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote: "Spread knowledge on Friday, for the danger of knowledge is forgetfulness, and send abundant blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) on Friday."

(The nineteenth occasion: when rising from a gathering)

Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id ibn Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, who said: I heard Sufyan ibn Sa'id, more than I can count, say when he wished to rise: "May Allah and His angels send blessings upon Muhammad, and upon the prophets of Allah and His angels." This is what I have seen of the narration on this occasion, and Allah knows best.

(The twentieth occasion: when passing by mosques and seeing them)

Al-Qadi Isma'il said in his book: Yahya ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Sayf ibn Umar al-Tamimi narrated to us from Sulayman al-Absi, from Ali ibn Husayn, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When you pass by a mosque, send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ)." [Its chain is mawquf and weak.]

(The twenty-first occasion: in times of anxiety, hardship, and seeking forgiveness)

Based on the hadith of Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father, who said: When two-thirds of the night had passed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rise and say: "O people, remember Allah! The quake has come, followed by the one that follows. Death has come with what it brings, death has come with what it brings." My father said: "O Messenger of Allah, I send abundant blessings upon you, so how much of my prayer should I make for you?" He said: "As much as you wish." I said: "A quarter?" He said: "As much as you wish, and if you increase it, it is better for you." I said: "A half?" He said: "As much as you wish, and if you increase it, it is better for you." I said: "Two-thirds?" He said: "As much as you wish, and if you increase it, it is better for you." I said: "I will make all my prayer for you." He said: "Then you will be relieved of your anxiety, and your sins will be forgiven." Al-Tirmidhi related it from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Tufayl, from his father, and said: [a hasan hadith].

He related another hadith from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Aqil also, from Tufayl, from his father, and authenticated it: "My likeness and the likeness of the prophets before me is like a man who built a house..." (the hadith). Ibn Abi Shaybah related it in his Musnad and abridged it, saying: from my father, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I make all my prayer a prayer upon you?" He said: "Then Allah will suffice you for what concerns you of the affairs of your worldly life and your Hereafter." (ﷺ), with abundant peace until the Day of Judgment.

(The twenty-second occasion: when writing his name (ﷺ))

Abu al-Shaykh said: Usayd ibn Asim narrated to us, Bishr ibn Ubayd narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the angels will continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as my name is in that book." Abu Musa said: "Several have related it from Usayd in this way." He said: "Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Allaf related it from Bishr ibn Ubayd, saying: from Hazim ibn Bakr, from Yazid ibn Iyad, from al-A'raj." It is also related from al-A'raj by routes other than these two.

On this topic there are also reports from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Ibn Abbas and Aishah (may Allah be pleased with them all).

Sulayman ibn al-Rabi' related: Kadih ibn Rahmah narrated to us, Nahshal ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the blessing will continue to be his as long as my name is in that book." [Weak.]

It was related by way of Ja'far ibn Ali al-Za'farani, who said: I heard my maternal uncle al-Hasan ibn Muhammad say: "I saw Ahmad ibn Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on him) in a dream, and he said to me: 'O Abu Ali, if you saw our blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in the books, how they would shine before us.'"

Abu al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Maymuni said: "I saw Shaykh Abu Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Uyaynah in a dream after his death, and on the fingers of his hands there was something written in gold-colored or saffron-colored ink. I asked him about it and said: 'O master, I see on your fingers something beautiful written, what is it?' He said: 'O my son, this is for my writing of the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)'; or he said: 'for my writing of (his name) (ﷺ) in the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).'"

Al-Khatib mentioned: Makki ibn Ali narrated to us, Abu Sulayman al-Harrani narrated to us, who said: A man from my neighbors, called Abu al-Fadl, who was abundant in fasting and prayer, said: "I used to write the hadith and not send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ). Then I saw him in a dream, and he said: 'When you write or mention (me), why do you not send blessings upon me?' Then I saw him once more, and he said to me: 'Your blessings upon me have reached me. So when you send blessings upon me, or mention (me), say (ﷺ).'"

Sufyan al-Thawri said: "If the person of hadith gained nothing but sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would still be receiving blessings (from Allah) for as long as that writing remains."

Muhammad ibn Abi Sulayman said: "I saw my father in a dream and said, 'O father, what has Allah done with you?' He said, 'He forgave me.' I said, 'For what?' He said, 'For my writing of the blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ).'"

One of the people of hadith said: "I had a neighbour who died, and he was seen in a dream. It was said to him, 'What has Allah done with you?' He said, 'He forgave me.' It was said, 'For what?' He said, 'Whenever I wrote the mention of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in a hadith, I wrote (ﷺ).'"

Sufyan ibn Uyayna said: "Khalaf, the owner of the worn-out garments, narrated to us: A friend of mine who used to seek hadith with me died. I saw him in my dream, wearing green garments and moving about in them. I said, 'Were you not with me, seeking hadith?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'What raised you to this?' He said, 'Whenever a hadith came up in which the mention of Muhammad (ﷺ) occurred, I would write (ﷺ) beneath it. So my Lord rewarded me with this which you see upon me.'"

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam said: "I saw al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, in a dream, and I said, 'What has Allah done with you?' He said, 'He had mercy on me, forgave me, and escorted me to Paradise as a bride is escorted, and showered me (with gifts) as a bride is showered.' I said, 'By what did you attain this state?' A speaker said to me, 'By what is in the book al-Risala (of the blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ)).' I said, 'How is that?' He said, 'And may Allah bless Muhammad as many times as those who remember him have remembered him, and as many times as the heedless have been heedless of remembering him.'" He said: "When I woke in the morning, I looked at the Risala and found the matter as I had seen (it in the dream)."

Al-Khatib said: "Bishr ibn Abd Allah al-Rumi informed us, saying: I heard al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Askari say: I heard Abu Ishaq al-Darimi, known as Nahshal, say: I used to write hadith, and in my transcription, when the Prophet (ﷺ) was mentioned, I would write the words 'said the Prophet (ﷺ), salutation (taslim)'. Then I saw the Prophet (ﷺ) in a dream, and it was as if he had taken something of what I had written, looked into it, and said, 'This is good.'"

Abdullah ibn Amr said: "Some of my brothers whom I trust narrated to me: I saw a man of the people of hadith in a dream and said, 'What has Allah done with you?' He said, 'He had mercy on me and forgave me.' I said, 'And why was that?' He said, 'Indeed, whenever I came upon the name of the Prophet (ﷺ), I wrote (ﷺ).'"

Muhammad ibn Salih mentioned it from Thawaba, from Sa'id ibn Marwan, from him.

Al-Hafiz Abu Musa has related in his book, from a group of the people of hadith, that they were seen after their deaths and informed that Allah the Exalted had forgiven them for their writing of the blessings upon the Prophet in every hadith.

Ibn Sinan said: "I heard Abbas al-Anbari and Ali ibn al-Madini say: We have never left off the blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in every hadith we heard. Sometimes we hurried, so we left spaces in the book in every hadith, until we returned to it."

(The twenty-third of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): when conveying knowledge to people, at reminders, narratives, delivering a lesson, and teaching knowledge, at its beginning and its end.)

Isma'il ibn Ishaq said in his book: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us, Husayn ibn Ali, that is al-Ju'fi, narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Burqan, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote: "To proceed: Some people have sought the world through works of the Hereafter, and among the storytellers some have introduced into their blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) an equivalent to their blessings upon their caliphs and their rulers. So when this letter of mine reaches you, command them that their blessings be upon the prophets and their supplication be for the Muslims in general, and that they leave off whatever is other than that."

The blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ) at this occasion is because it is an occasion for conveying the knowledge he brought, spreading it among his community, presenting it to them, and calling them to his sunnah and his way (ﷺ). This is among the best of deeds and the greatest in benefit for the servant in this world and the Hereafter.

(The twenty-fourth of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): the beginning and end of the day.)

Al-Tabarani said: Hafs ibn Umar al-Sabbah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih al-Jurjusi narrated to us, Baqiyya ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Alhani narrated to me, who said: I heard Khalid ibn Ma'dan narrate from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me in the morning ten times, and in the evening ten times, my intercession will reach him on the Day of Resurrection."

Abu Musa al-Madini said: "More than one narrated it from Baqiyya, and Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih used to live in Homs near the church of Jirjis, so he was attributed to it."

(The twenty-fifth of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): following a sin when one wishes to have it expiated.)

Ibn Abi Asim said in his book, "The Blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ)": al-Hasan ibn al-Bazzar narrated to us, Shababa narrated to us, Mughira ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send blessings upon me, for sending blessings upon me is an expiation for you. Whoever sends blessings upon me once, Allah will send blessings upon him ten times."

Ibn Abi Asim also said in his book: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Ata narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Manzur, from Ibn Mu'adh, from Abu Kahil, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O Abu Kahil, whoever sends blessings upon me three times each day and three times each night, out of love and longing for me, it will be incumbent upon Allah to forgive his sins on that night and that day."

Abu al-Shaykh said in his book, "The Blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ)": Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Nasr narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Yazid narrated to us, He said: al-Husayn ibn Hafs narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Nafi' ibn Ka'b al-Madini, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send blessings upon me, for sending blessings upon me is a purification (zakat) for you." Ibn Abi Shayba also narrated it from Ibn Fudayl, from Layth ibn Ka'b, from Abu Hurayra.

So this contains reports that the blessing is a purification (zakat) for the one who sends it upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and zakat implies growth, blessing and cleanliness; and the previous one contains that it is an expiation, which implies the erasure of sin. Thus the two hadiths together establish that by blessing upon him (ﷺ) the soul attains purity from its vices, and growth and increase in its perfections and virtues is established for it, and the perfection of the soul returns to these two matters. It is known that there is no perfection of the soul except through blessing upon the Prophet (ﷺ), which is among the requirements of love for him, following him, and giving him precedence over every created being (ﷺ).

(The twenty-sixth of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): when poverty befalls or there is fear of its occurrence.)

Abu Nu'aym said: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sammaa narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Fitr ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Samura al-Sawa'i, from his father, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when a man came to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, which deeds are closest to Allah, mighty and majestic?" He said: "Truthfulness in speech and fulfilling trusts." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase for us." He said: "Night prayer and fasting in the scorching heat." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase for us." He said: "Frequent remembrance (of Allah), and blessing upon me, which removes poverty." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, increase for us." He said: "Whoever leads a people in prayer, let him make it light, for among them are the elderly, the sick, the weak, and the one with need."

(The twenty-seventh of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): when a man proposes to a woman in marriage.)

Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾. He said: That is, Allah the Exalted praises your Prophet and forgives him, and commands the angels to seek forgiveness for him. ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾. Praise him in your prayers, in your mosques, in every occasion, and in the marriage sermon for women, so do not forget him.

(The twenty-eighth of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): upon sneezing.)

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Hadrami narrated to us, Sahl ibn Salih al-Antaki narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Nafi', who said: I saw Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, when a man sneezed beside him, and he said: "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon the Messenger of Allah."

Ibn Umar said: "I too say, 'Peace upon the Messenger of Allah,' but it is not like this that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us. He commanded us that when we sneeze we say: 'Praise be to Allah in every state.'"

Al-Tabarani said: No one narrated it from Sa'id except al-Walid, and Sahl was alone in it.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Humayd Mas'ada: Ziyad ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, Hadrami, client of the family of al-Jarud, narrated to us, from Nafi', that a man sneezed beside Ibn Umar and said, "Praise be to Allah, and peace upon the Messenger of Allah." Ibn Umar said: "I say, 'Praise be to Allah, and peace upon the Messenger of Allah,' but it is not like this that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us. He taught us to say: 'Praise be to Allah in every state.'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a gharib hadith, which we know only through the hadith of Ziyad ibn al-Rabi'.

Abu Musa al-Madini said: It is also narrated from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, the opposite of that. Then he cited through the chain of Abd Allah ibn Ahmad: Abbad ibn Ziyad al-Asadi narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nafi', who said: A man sneezed beside Ibn Umar, and Ibn Umar said to him: "You have been stingy! Why did you not praise Allah the Exalted and send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ)?" A group, among them Abu Musa al-Madini and others, adopted this view, and others disputed with them on this and said: Sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) is not recommended upon sneezing; rather it is the place for praising Allah alone, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prescribed upon sneezing only praise of Allah the Exalted. And sending blessings upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), although it is among the best deeds and most beloved to Allah the Exalted, each remembrance has a place specific to it which nothing else can fill.

They said: For this reason, blessings upon him (ﷺ) are not prescribed in bowing, prostration, or the standing of rising from bowing, but are prescribed in the final tashahhud, either as a prescription of obligation or of recommendation. They also narrated a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not mention me at three times: at naming the food, at slaughtering, and upon sneezing."

This hadith is not sound, for it is from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Isa al-Sijzi, from Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd al-Ammi, from Kathir, from Uwayd, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned it. It has three defects. The first: Sulayman ibn Isa was alone in it. Al-Bayhaqi said: He is among those who fabricate hadith. The second: the weakness of Abd al-Rahim al-Ammi. The third: its disconnection.

Al-Bayhaqi said: We have related regarding blessings upon the Prophet at sneezing what Abu Tahir al-Faqih informed us: Abu Abd Allah al-Saffar informed us, Abd Allah al-Saffar narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, Abbad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, and he mentioned the hadith previously cited.

(The twenty-ninth of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): after finishing ablution.)

Abu al-Shaykh said in his book: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim ibn Shabib narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jabir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you finishes his purification, let him say: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger,' then let him send blessings upon me. When he says that, the gates of mercy are opened for him." This is a well-known hadith with chains from Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uqba ibn Amir, Thawban, and Anas, may Allah be pleased with them all, and in none of them is there mention of blessing except in this narration. [[A weak hadith]]

Ibn Abi Asim said in his book: Duhaym narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, Abd al-Muhaymin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, raising it: "There is no ablution for one who does not send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ)." Abd al-Muhaymin is not relied upon as evidence, and the hadith has been mentioned earlier.

(The thirtieth of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): upon entering the house.)

Mentioned by al-Hafiz Abu Musa al-Madini, and he related in it a hadith from Abu Salih ibn al-Muhallab, from Abu Bakr ibn Imran, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Walid narrated to me, Amr ibn Sa'id narrated to me, Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ajlan narrated to me, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained to him of poverty and narrowness of livelihood. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "When you enter your house, greet (with salam) if there is anyone in it or if there is no one in it, then send blessings upon me, and recite: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One﴾ once." The man did so, and Allah made his provision abundant until it overflowed to his neighbours and relatives.

(The thirty-first of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): in every gathering in which the remembrance of Allah the Exalted takes place.)

From the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, Allah has wandering angels who, when they pass by gatherings of remembrance, say to one another: 'Sit down.' When the people supplicate, they say 'Amin' to their supplication. When they send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), they send blessings with them until they finish. Then some say to others: 'Blessed are these people; they return forgiven.'"

The origin of this hadith is in Muslim, and this is the wording of Muslim ibn Ibrahim al-Kishshi, who narrated to us: Abd al-Salam ibn Ajlan narrated to us, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi narrated to us, from Abu Hurayra, and he mentioned it.

(The thirty-second of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): when one forgets something or wishes to recall it.)

Mentioned by Abu Musa al-Madini, and he related in it through the chain of Muhammad ibn Attab al-Marwazi: Sa'dan ibn Abda Abu Sa'id al-Marwazi narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah al-Atakī informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you forget something, send blessings upon me, and you will remember it, if Allah wills." The Hafiz said: I have mentioned it from other than this chain in the book "Memorization and Forgetfulness."

(The thirty-third of the occasions for blessing upon him (ﷺ): when a need presents itself to the servant.)

Ahmad ibn Musa al-Hafiz said: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Usayd narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Yazid narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath al-Khurasani narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Sinan ibn Uqba ibn Abi A'isha al-Madani narrated to us, from Abu Sahl ibn Malik, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me one hundred times when he prays the dawn prayer, before speaking, Allah will fulfil for him one hundred needs: thirty of them He will hasten for him, and seventy He will delay for him. And in the evening prayer it is likewise." They said: "How should the blessing upon you be, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace."

"O Allah, bless him, until you count one hundred times."

**Ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه) said:** "When you wish to ask for a need, begin with praise (al-madha), glorification (al-tahmid), and extolling God, the Mighty and Majestic, with what is worthy of Him. Then send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and then make your supplication. This is more likely to bring about the attainment of your need."

**Al-Tabarani said:** Sahl ibn Musa narrated to us: Zurayq ibn al-Suht narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata narrated to us: Fa'id Abu al-Warqa' narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa narrated to us: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'Whoever has a need with God, the Mighty and Majestic, let him perform ablution and perfect the ablution, let him pray two rak'ahs, let him praise God, the Mighty and Majestic, let him send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), and let him say: "There is no god but God, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to God, Lord of the Mighty Throne. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask You for that which necessitates Your mercy, for the resolutions of Your forgiveness, for the gain of every righteousness and the safety from every sin. Leave no worry of mine except that You relieve it, no sin except that You forgive it, and no need which is pleasing to You except that You fulfil it, O Most Merciful of the merciful."'"

**Ibn Mandah al-Hafiz said:** Abd al-Samad al-Asimi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mustamli informed us: Muhammad ibn Darastuyah narrated to us: Sahl ibn Mutawayh narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ubayd narrated to us: Abbas ibn Bakkar narrated to us: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to us, from Jabir (رضي الله عنه), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever sends blessings upon me a hundred times each day, God will fulfil for him a hundred needs: seventy of them for his Hereafter and thirty of them for his worldly life."

Al-Hafiz Abu Musa al-Madini said: "This is a good (hasan) hadith."

I say: The hadith of Fudala ibn Ubayd and Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning this has already been mentioned.

**(The thirty-fourth of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): at the ringing of the ear)**

Mentioned by Abu Musa and others.

Ibn Asim said in his book: Abu al-Rabi' narrated to us: Hassan ibn Adi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi' narrated to us, from his brother Abd Allah, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the ear of one of you rings, let him send blessings upon me, and let him say: 'Remember God with good (dhikr Allah bi-khayr) for whoever remembered me.'"

Ma'mar ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Rafi' also narrated it, from his father, from his grandfather, without mentioning Abd Allah in the isnad. In one narration: "God remembers whoever remembered me with good."

**(The thirty-fifth of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): after the prayers)**

Mentioned by al-Hafiz Abu Musa and others, and they mentioned nothing on this except an account which Abu Musa al-Madini related by way of Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Isma'il ibn Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-Hasib say: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar informed me, who said: I was with Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid when al-Shibli came. Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid stood up to him, embraced him, and kissed between his eyes. I said to him: "O my master, you do this with al-Shibli, while you and all of Baghdad regard him as insane?" He said to me: "I did with him what I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) do with him. I saw the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in a dream, and al-Shibli approached, and he stood up for him and kissed between his eyes. I said: 'O Messenger of God, do you do this with al-Shibli?' He said: 'He recites after his prayer: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128], to its end, and follows it with sending blessings upon me.'"

In another narration: he never prayed an obligatory prayer without reciting after it ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ to the end of the surah, and saying three times: "May God bless you, O Muhammad (ṣallā llāhu 'alayka yā Muḥammad)." He said: When al-Shibli entered, I asked him about what he recites after the prayer, and he mentioned the same.

**(The thirty-sixth of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): at the slaughter of an animal)**

This matter has been disputed. Al-Shafi'i (raḥimahu Allah) regarded it as recommended, and said: "The saying of the basmalah over the slaughtered animal, 'In the name of God,' is required; if one adds some other remembrance of God, the addition is good. I do not dislike, together with mentioning God's name over the slaughtered animal, saying 'May God bless the Messenger of God'; rather I like it for him, and I like to increase sending blessings in all circumstances, because remembering God by sending blessings upon Him is faith in God and an act of worship for which the one who says it is rewarded, God willing."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf mentioned that he was with the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) went ahead of him. Abd al-Rahman followed him in prostration, and the Prophet (ﷺ) stood waiting for him and prolonged it, then raised his head. Abd al-Rahman said: "I feared that God had taken your soul during your prostration." He said: "O Abd al-Rahman, when I was in the place where you saw me, Jibril (ʿalayhi al-salam) met me and informed me from God that He said: 'Whoever sends blessings upon you, I bless him,' so I prostrated to God in thanks." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever forgets to send blessings upon me has strayed from the path of Paradise." Ibn al-Qayyim (raḥimahu Allah) elaborated on this matter at length.

Others disputed this with him, among them the companions of Imam Abu Hanifa (raḥimahu Allah), for they disliked sending blessings in this situation. This was mentioned by the author of al-Muhit, who gave as the reason that in it there is "al-ihlal" (raising the voice) for other than God, the Exalted.

The companions of Imam Ahmad (raḥimahu Allah) differed: al-Qadi and his companions disliked it, and Abu al-Khattab mentioned the dislike in his "Ru'us al-Masa'il". Ibn Shaqila said: it is recommended, as the saying of al-Shafi'i.

Those who disliked it argued: Abu Muhammad al-Khallal narrated with his isnad from Mu'adh ibn Jabal (رضي الله عنه), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Two places in which I have no share: at sneezing and at slaughter."

They also relied on the hadith of Sulayman ibn Isa al-Sajzi, from Abd al-Rahim ibn Zayd al-Ammi, from his father. The discussion of this hadith has already been mentioned, and that it is not established.

**(The thirty-seventh of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): during the prayer, other than in the tashahhud)**

Rather, in the state of recitation, when one passes by mention of him, or by the saying of God, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾.

Mentioned by our companions and others. They said: whenever one passes by his mention during recitation, he stops and sends blessings upon him.

Isma'il ibn Ishaq narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us: Bishr ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: "If he passes by the mention of sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), let him stop and send blessings upon him in voluntary prayer."

Imam Ahmad (raḥimahu Allah) stated this explicitly, saying: "If the one praying passes by a verse in which there is mention of the Prophet (ﷺ), then if it is a voluntary (nafl) prayer, he sends blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ)."

**(The thirty-eighth of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): in place of charity)**

For one who has no wealth, sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) suffices in place of charity for the one in hardship.

Ibn Wahb said, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj Abu al-Samh, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id (رضي الله عنه), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does not have charity with him, let him say in his supplication: 'O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, and send blessings upon the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women,' for it is for him a purification (zakat)." It was narrated by his nephew (ibn akhihi) and Harun ibn Ma'ruf from him.

**(The thirty-ninth of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): upon sleeping)**

Abu al-Shaykh said in his book: Ishaq ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki narrated to us: Adam Abu Iyas narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Nashr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Amir narrated to us, who said: Abu Qarsafa said: "I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Whoever goes to his bed, then recites ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾ [al-Mulk: 1], then says: "O God, Lord of the Sacred Precinct (al-Hill) and the Sacred Sanctuary (al-Haram), Lord of the city of the Sacred House, Lord of the Corner and the Station, Lord of the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram), by the right of every verse You sent down in the month of Ramadan, convey to the spirit of Muhammad (ﷺ) from me a greeting and peace," four times, God will assign two angels to him until they come to Muhammad (ﷺ), and they say to him: "O Muhammad, so-and-so son of so-and-so sends you greetings and the mercy of God," and he says: "And upon so-and-so from me is peace, the mercy of God and His blessings.'"

Al-Hafiz Abu Musa said: Nashr, the father of Muhammad, is with a fatha on the nun.

I say: Abu Qarsafa was mentioned by Ibn Abd al-Barr in his book "al-Sahaba", and he said: his name is Jundurah, from the Banu Kinana, he had companionship (suhba) with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he dwelt in Palestine. It was also said that he used to live in Tihama. But this Muhammad ibn Nashr is the Madinan, of whom al-Azdi said: "abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith), unknown (majhul)."

I say: The defect of the hadith is that it is known as a saying of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, and this is more likely; and God knows best.

**(The fortieth of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): at every matter of importance (kull kalam dhi bal))**

For one begins with praising God and extolling Him, then with sending blessings upon His Messenger (ﷺ), then mentions his speech after that.

As for beginning with praise: it is because of what is in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Abu Hurayra (رضي الله عنه), from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he said: "Every speech in which one does not begin with praise of God is amputated (ajdham)."

As for sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ): Abu Musa al-Madini narrated from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Yunus ibn Yazid, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra (رضي الله عنه), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Every speech in which God is not mentioned, and which does not begin with Him and with blessings upon me, is cut off (aqta'), deprived of every blessing." [[Its isnad is weak]]

**(The forty-first of the occasions for sending blessings upon him (ﷺ): in the course of the Eid prayer)**

It is recommended that one praise God, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ).

Isma'il ibn Ishaq said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hisham al-Dastawa'i narrated to us: Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Alqama, that Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Musa and Hudhayfa were visited by al-Walid ibn Uqba one day before the Eid, and he said to them: "The Eid has drawn near, so how is the takbir in it?" Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "You begin, and say takbir, one takbir with which you open the prayer, and praise your Lord and send blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ), then supplicate, and say takbir and do the same; then say takbir and do the same; then recite, then say takbir and bow; then rise, recite, praise your Lord, send blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), then supplicate and do the same; then say takbir and do the same; then say takbir and do the same, then bow." Hudhayfa and Abu Musa said: "Abu Abd al-Rahman has spoken truly." [[Its isnad is good]]

In this hadith there is the continuity between the two recitations (al-muwala bayna al-qira'atayn), which is the position of Abu Hanifa and one of the two narrations from Ahmad. In it are the extra takbirs of the Eid, three by three, which is the position of Abu Hanifa. In it is praise of God and blessings upon His Messenger between the takbirs, which is the position of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. Abu Hanifa adopted it regarding the number of takbirs and the continuity between the two recitations; Ahmad and al-Shafi'i adopted it regarding the recommendation of remembrance between the takbirs. Abu Hanifa and Malik hold that the takbirs should be recited in succession without remembrance between them; Malik did not adopt it in this matter or in that. And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.

**(Section: on the benefits and fruits achieved by sending blessings upon him (ﷺ))**

The first: compliance with the command of God, glorified and exalted.

The second: agreement with Him, glorified, in sending blessings upon him (ﷺ). Although the two blessings differ, our blessing upon him is supplication and request, and God's blessing upon him is praise and honouring, as has been mentioned.

The third: agreement with His angels in it.

The fourth: the obtaining of ten blessings from God upon the one who prays once.

The fifth: that he is raised ten degrees.

The sixth: that ten good deeds are recorded for him.

The seventh: that ten sins are erased from him.

The eighth: that the answering of his supplication is hoped for when he places it before it, for it ascends (tusa'id) the supplication to the presence of the Lord of the worlds.

The ninth: that it is a cause of his intercession (ﷺ), when he combines it with asking for the Wasila for him, or singles it out, as has been mentioned in the hadith of Ruwayfi' concerning that.

The tenth: that it is a cause of the forgiveness of sins, as has been mentioned.

The eleventh: that it is a cause of God's sufficing the servant in what concerns him.

The twelfth: that it is a cause of the servant's nearness to him (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection, and the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه) concerning that has been mentioned.

The thirteenth: that it takes the place of charity for the one in hardship.

The fourteenth: that it is a cause of the fulfilment of needs.

The fifteenth: that it is a cause of God's blessing upon the one who prays, and His angels' blessing upon him.

The sixteenth: that it is a purification (zakat) for the one who prays and a cleansing for him.

The seventeenth: that it is a cause of the servant being given glad tidings of Paradise before his death. Al-Hafiz Abu Musa mentioned this in his book and mentioned a hadith concerning it.

The eighteenth: that it is a cause of salvation from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. Abu Musa mentioned it and mentioned a hadith concerning it.

The nineteenth: that it is a cause of the Prophet's (ﷺ) returning the blessing and peace upon the one who prays and the one who greets him.

The twentieth: that it is a cause of the servant's remembrance of what he has forgotten, as has been mentioned.

The twenty-first: that it is a cause of the goodness of the gathering, and that it does not become a regret for its people on the Day of Resurrection.

The twenty-second: that it is a cause of the negation of poverty, as has been mentioned.

The twenty-third: that it removes from the servant the name of stinginess (bukhl) when he sends blessings upon him at the mention of him (ﷺ).

The twenty-fourth: that it casts its owner onto the path of Paradise, and it misses for the one who abandons it from its path.

The twenty-fifth: that it saves from the stench of a gathering in which God and His Messenger are not mentioned, and in which He is not praised and extolled, and upon His Messenger (ﷺ) blessings are not sent.

The twenty-sixth: that it is a cause of the completion of the speech which was begun with praise of God and blessings upon His Messenger.

The twenty-seventh: that it is a cause of the abundance of the servant's light upon the Sirat; and there is a hadith concerning it, mentioned by Abu Musa and others.

The twenty-eighth: that by it the servant is removed from coarseness (al-jafa').

The twenty-ninth: that it is a cause of God, glorified, preserving a good reputation for the one who sends blessings upon him among the inhabitants of heaven and earth, because the one who prays asks God to praise His Messenger, honour him and exalt him, and recompense is of the kind of the deed; so it is necessary that the one who prays attains some measure of that.

The thirtieth: that it is a cause of blessing in the person of the one who prays, his deeds, his life, and the causes of his welfare, because the one who prays supplicates his Lord to bless him and his family, and this supplication is answered, and recompense is of its kind.

The thirty-first: that it is a cause of attaining God's mercy for him, because mercy is either in the sense of blessing, as a group has said, or among its necessary consequences and requirements according to the correct view; so the one who prays for him must attain a mercy that reaches him.

The Thirty-Second Benefit: that it is a cause for the continuance of love for the Messenger (ﷺ), its increase and its multiplication. This is one of the knots of faith, which is not complete without it. For the servant, whenever he frequently remembers the beloved and brings him to mind, and brings to mind his excellences and the meanings that draw love to him, his love is multiplied, his longing for him grows, and it takes hold of his whole heart. And when he turns away from remembering him and from calling his excellences to his heart, his love diminishes in his heart. Nothing refreshes the eye of the lover more than seeing his beloved, and nothing refreshes his heart more than remembering him and bringing his excellences to mind. When this becomes strong in his heart, his tongue flows with praising him, extolling him and mentioning his excellences. The increase and decrease of this follow the increase and decrease of love in his heart, and experience bears witness to this. So much so that some poets said about this:

*"I am astonished at the one who says, 'I remembered my love.' Could I forget, that I should remember the one I have forgotten?"*

So this lover marvels at the one who says, "I remembered my beloved," because remembrance comes after forgetting, and if his love were complete he would not forget his beloved.

Another said:

*"I wish to forget her remembrance, but it is as though Layla presents herself to me on every path."*

So this one informs about himself that his love for her prevents him from forgetting her.

Another said:

*"The heart is asked to forget you, but the natures refuse to be transferred."*

So he informs that their love and their remembrance have become his nature, and whoever wants him to do otherwise, his nature refuses to be removed from him. The well-known proverb says: whoever loves something remembers it much. And in this most noble court, the most fitting of what has been recited is:

*"Were my heart split open, in its midst would be your remembrance, and the Tawhid written in a line."*

This is the heart of the believer: the Tawhid of Allah and the remembrance of His Messenger are written in it, and no erasure or removal can reach them. Since frequent remembrance of a thing necessitates the continuance of love for it, and forgetting it is a cause for the loss or weakening of love, and since Allah, glory be to Him, is the one deserving from His servants the utmost love together with the utmost veneration, indeed the shirk that Allah does not forgive is to associate others with Him in love and veneration, so that one loves another and venerates another of the creatures as he loves and venerates Allah the Exalted. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among the people are those who take, besides Allah, equals whom they love as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165].

So He informed, glory be to Him, that the polytheist loves the rival as he loves Allah the Exalted, and that the believer is more intense in love for Allah than anything else. And the people of the Fire said in the Fire: ﴿By Allah, we were certainly in manifest error when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 97-98].

And it is known that they only equated them with Him, glory be to Him, in love, in devotion and in worship. Otherwise, no one ever said that the idol or other rivals were equal to the Lord of the worlds in His attributes, in His actions, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, or in the creation of His servants. Rather, the equality was only in love and worship.

And more astray than these, and worse in condition, is the one who equates everything with Allah, glory be to Him, in existence, and makes the existence of every existent, whether perfect or imperfect, to be His existence. If Allah has judged as astray and wretched the one who equated Him with the idols in love, while they believed in the vast difference between Allah and His creation in essence, attributes and actions, then how about the one who equates Allah with existents in all of that, and claims that he worships nothing but Allah in every object of worship?

The purpose is that since continuous remembrance is a cause for continuous love, and since Allah, glory be to Him, is most deserving of perfect love, worship, veneration and exaltation, frequent remembrance of Him is among the most beneficial things for the servant, and his enemy is truly the one who prevents him from remembering his Lord and from worshipping Him. For this reason Allah, glory be to Him, commanded frequent remembrance of Him in the Qur'an and made it a cause of success. He the Exalted said: ﴿And remember Allah often that you may succeed﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 10].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿And the men who remember Allah often and the women who remember﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth and your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9].

And He the Exalted said: ﴿So remember Me; I will remember you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 152].

And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The mufarridun have outstripped." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who are the mufarridun?" He said: "Those who remember Allah much, and the women who remember."

And in al-Tirmidhi, from Abu al-Darda' (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Shall I not tell you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them with your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, better for you than spending gold and silver, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks while they strike yours?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The remembrance of Allah the Exalted." [Its chain is sound.] It is also in the Muwatta' as a statement of Abu al-Darda' (mawquf).

Mu'adh ibn Jabal said: "No son of Adam has done a deed that saves him from the punishment of Allah more than the remembrance of Allah and the remembrance of His Messenger (ﷺ), which follows it."

The purpose is that continuous remembrance is a cause of continuous love. So remembrance to the heart is like water to the crop, indeed like water to the fish, which has no life except by it.

And its kinds are: first, remembering Him by His names and attributes and praising Him by them. Second, glorifying Him (tasbih), praising Him (tahmid), magnifying Him (takbir), declaring His oneness (tahlil) and glorifying Him (tamjid); the commonly used sense of the word "dhikr" among later scholars is this. Third, remembering Him by His rulings, commands and prohibitions, and this is the remembrance of the scholar. Indeed, the three kinds are their remembrance of their Lord.

And among the best forms of His remembrance is remembering Him by His speech. He the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾ [Ta-Ha: 124].

So His remembrance here is His speech which He sent down upon His Messenger (ﷺ).

And He the Exalted said: ﴿Those who believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah are hearts assured﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 28].

And among His remembrance, glory be to Him, is supplication to Him, seeking His forgiveness and humbling oneself before Him. So these are five kinds of remembrance.

The Thirty-Third Benefit: that sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) is a cause for his love for the servant. For if it is a cause for the increase of the love of the one who sends blessings upon him for him, then likewise it is a cause for his love for the one who sends blessings upon him (ﷺ).

The Thirty-Fourth Benefit: that it is a cause for the guidance of the servant and the life of his heart. For whenever he increases in sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) and remembering him, and his love takes hold of his heart, until no opposition remains in his heart to any of his commands and no doubt about anything he brought, rather what he brought becomes written and inscribed in his heart, which he continues to read through the successive states of his life, and he draws from it guidance, success and various kinds of knowledge. And whenever he grows in insight, strength and knowledge in this, his blessings upon him (ﷺ) increase.

For this reason, the prayer upon him by the people of knowledge who are acquainted with his sunnah and his guidance and who follow him is different from the prayer upon him by the common people, whose share of it is only moving their limbs and raising their voices. As for his followers who know his sunnah and his guidance and follow him, unlike the common people, whose share of it is moving their limbs and raising their voices, and as for his followers who know his sunnah and are aware of what he brought, their blessings upon him are of another kind. Whenever they increase in knowledge of what he brought, they increase in love for him, and in knowledge of the reality of the prayer upon him that is required of them by Allah the Exalted.

Likewise, the remembrance of Allah, glory be to Him: whenever the servant knows Him more, obeys Him more and loves Him more, his remembrance is different from the remembrance of the heedless and the distracted. And this is a matter known only by experience and not by mere report. There is a difference between one who mentions the attributes of his beloved, whose love has taken possession of his whole heart, and praises him and glorifies him by them, and one who mentions them merely as a sign or as words whose meaning he does not understand, his heart not agreeing with his tongue. Just as there is a difference between the wailing of a mourner and the weeping of a bereaved mother. So his remembrance (ﷺ), and the remembrance of what he brought, and praising Allah, glory be to Him, for His favour upon us and His grace in sending him, is the life of existence and its spirit, as it has been said:

*"The spirit of gatherings is his remembrance and his speech, and guidance for every bewildered one who is lost."*

*"And when he is absent from a gathering, those are the dead among the living."*

The Thirty-Fifth Benefit: that it is a cause for the name of the one who prays upon him (ﷺ) to be presented to him and for him to be mentioned in his presence, as previously mentioned in his saying: "Your prayers are presented to me."

And his saying (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah has appointed angels at my grave who convey to me the greetings of my community." And it is sufficient for a servant to have his name mentioned with goodness before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And it has been said regarding this meaning:

*"And whoever has a thought come to him is worthy that it should precede him."*

And another said:

*"Welcome to what I was not worthy of reaching, the words of the bringer of good news after despair, that of relief."*

*"Glad tidings to you! Take off what is upon you, for you have been mentioned, and what is in you of crookedness."*

The Thirty-Sixth Benefit: that it is a cause for the firmness of the foot upon the Sirat and for crossing over it, based on the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, which Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated from him, concerning the dream of the Prophet (ﷺ), in which: "I saw a man of my community crawling upon the Sirat, sometimes crawling on his hands and knees and sometimes clinging, and my blessings came to him and set him upon his feet and rescued him." Abu Musa al-Madini narrated it, and built his book al-Targhib wal-Tarhib upon it, and said: "This is a very good (hasan) hadith."

The Thirty-Seventh Benefit: that sending blessings upon him (ﷺ) is the discharge of the least of his rights and thanks to him for his favour which Allah has bestowed upon us. Yet what he deserves of that cannot be counted in knowledge, power or will. But Allah, glory be to Him, in His generosity, is content from His servants with a little of their gratitude and the discharge of His right.

The Thirty-Eighth Benefit: that it includes the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, His thanks, and knowledge of His favour upon His servants by sending him. So the one who sends blessings upon him (ﷺ) has in his prayer upon him included the remembrance of Allah and the remembrance of His Messenger, and the request that He reward him for his prayer upon him with what He deserves, just as we have come to know our Lord and His names and attributes, and He guided us to the path of His pleasure, and made us know what is ours after reaching Him and coming before Him. So it includes all of faith. Indeed, it includes acknowledgement of the Lord who is called upon, His existence, His knowledge, His hearing, His power, His will, His life, His speech, the sending of His Messenger, and the confirmation of all his reports, and the perfection of love for Him. And there is no doubt that these are the foundations of faith. So the prayer upon him (ﷺ) includes the servant's knowledge of all this, his affirmation of it, and his love for it. Therefore it is among the best of deeds.

The Thirty-Ninth Benefit: that the prayer upon him (ﷺ) from the servant is a supplication, and the supplication and request of the servant from his Lord is of two kinds.

The first: his request for his needs and urgent matters and what befalls him by night and by day. This is supplication and request and preference for what the servant loves and seeks.

The second: his request that He praise His beloved and friend, increase his honour, his dignity and his preference, and raise his remembrance and his rank. There is no doubt that Allah the Exalted loves this, and His Messenger loves it. So the one who sends blessings upon him (ﷺ) has directed his request, his desire and his seeking towards what Allah and His Messenger love, and has preferred that over seeking his own needs and loves. Indeed, this sought matter is among the things most beloved to him and most preferred by him. So he has preferred what Allah and His Messenger love over what he himself loves, and has preferred Allah and what He loves over everything else. And the reward is of the kind of the deed. So whoever prefers Allah over others, Allah prefers him over others. Consider this by what people observe when they seek to draw near to their kings and leaders and to gain status with them. They ask the one obeyed to bestow favour upon the one they know to be the most beloved of his subjects to him. And whenever they ask him to increase his gift, his honour and his dignity, their rank with him rises, their closeness to him increases, and they gain his favour, because they know from him the desire to bestow favour, dignity and honour upon his beloved. So the one most beloved to him is the one who asks him most and desires most that His favour and kindness be completed upon him. This is a matter observed by the senses. And the status of these people and the status of the one whose needs are the king's own concern, while he is free from asking, are not equal. The honouring of the beloved and the bestowing of favour upon him is one; how much more so with the greatest lover and the most noble of lovers, for the most noble Beloved, and the one most deserving of love from his Lord.
