And had there been no benefit of the prayer upon him except this sought matter alone, it would have sufficed the believer for honour.

Here is a fine point for the one who teaches his community their religion and what he brought, calls them to it, urges them towards it, and is patient in that: the Prophet (ﷺ) has a reward beyond the reward of his own deeds, equal to the rewards of those who followed him. So the one who calls to his sunnah and religion, and the good teacher of the community, if he intends to bestow this share upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and direct it to him, and his purpose in calling people to Allah is to draw near to Him by guiding His servants, and to bestow upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the rewards of those who obey him, together with giving them their rewards in full, he will have a reward in his calling and his teaching according to this intention. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.

(Fasl)

Among the ways Satan toys with the Jews is that they slander the prophets and harm them.

They harmed Musa (peace be upon him) during his lifetime and attributed to him what Allah the Exalted had cleared him of. Allah, glory be to Him, forbade this Ummah from imitating them in that when He says: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honoured in the sight of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 69].

It is established in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, each looking at the private parts of the others. Musa (peace be upon him) used to bathe alone, so the Children of Israel said: 'By Allah, nothing prevents Musa from bathing with us except that he has a hernia (adar).' So Musa went to bathe, and he placed his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment. Musa set off after it, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until the Children of Israel saw the private parts of Musa, and they said: 'By Allah, there is no defect in Musa.' The rock stopped, and he took his garment and began striking the rock." Abu Hurayrah said: "By Allah, there are indeed six or seven marks on the rock from the striking of Musa." And Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said﴾, to the end of the verse.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id: "The Children of Israel said: 'Musa has a hernia (adar).' Another group said: 'He has leprosy (abras), because of how intensely he concealed himself.'"

Ibn Sirin said, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (peace be upon him): "Musa was a man of great modesty and concealment; hardly any of his skin could be seen, out of shyness. Those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He conceals himself to this extent only because of a defect in his skin: either leprosy, or a hernia, or some ailment.' And Allah the Exalted wished to clear him of what they said." And he mentioned the hadith.

Sufyan ibn Husayn said, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Jubayr, from al-Hakam ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, concerning the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Do not be like those who harmed Musa﴾.

He said: "Musa and Harun ascended the mountain, and Harun died. The Children of Israel said: 'You killed him, for he loved us more than you did and was gentler to us than you were.' And they harmed him with this. So Allah the Exalted commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed by the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death until the Children of Israel knew that he had died. Then Allah the Exalted cleared him of that, and they took him away and buried him, and no one among the creation of Allah the Exalted witnessed his grave except the vulture (al-rakhm), so Allah the Exalted made it deaf and mute."

[Section: Making excuses for creation is partly praiseworthy and partly blameworthy]

As for seeking excuses for creation, this has two aspects: a praiseworthy aspect and a blameworthy, forbidden aspect.

The blameworthy aspect is that you seek their excuses by looking only at the divine decree (al-qadar) and its operation over them, whether they wish it or not, so that you excuse them by the decree.

Many of the wayfarers (al-salikin) and of those who contemplate the decree, who are annihilated in witnessing it, arrive at this decree. As has already been mentioned, it is a very perilous path, of little benefit, and it does not save by itself.

I think this is what the author of *al-Manazil* (Sahib al-Manazil) meant, because he said after that:

"The servant's witnessing of the (divine) ruling leaves him no appreciation of any good deed nor disapproval of any evil deed, because he ascends from all meanings to the meaning of the ruling."

This witnessing is an incomplete and blameworthy witnessing. If its possessor follows it through, and so excuses the enemies of Allah and the people who oppose Him and His messengers, and seeks excuses for them, he becomes opposed to Allah in His command, excusing one whom Allah has not excused, and seeking the excuse of one whom Allah has condemned and commanded to be blamed. This is not agreement with Allah. Rather, agreeing with Him is to blame this person and to believe that he has no excuse before Allah or in reality. Allah, mighty and majestic, has already offered him an excuse and completely removed his excuse. If he were truly excused before Allah in reality, He would never punish him at all, for Allah, mighty and majestic, is too merciful, too self-sufficient, and too just to punish one who has an excuse. No one loves excuses more than Allah, and for this reason He sent the messengers and revealed the books, to remove the excuses of His creation, so that they would have no proof against Him.

It is known that one who seeks their excuse and validates it maintains a proof which Allah has invalidated in every respect. "To Allah belongs the conclusive proof" (cf. 6:149). As for those among His creation who have an excuse, such as the child who cannot discern, the mentally deficient, one who has not received the call, and the deaf and blind who neither see nor hear, Allah does not punish these without sin at all. For them there is another ruling in the Hereafter: He tests them by sending a messenger to them who commands and forbids them. Whoever among them obeys the messenger, He admits into Paradise, and whoever disobeys him, He admits into the Fire. Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari related this from the People of the Sunnah and Hadith in his *Maqalat*, and there are several hadiths on it, some of which are in the *Musnad* of Ahmad, such as the hadith of al-Aswad ibn Sari' and the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

As for one who casts doubt on these hadiths on the grounds that the Hereafter is a place of recompense and not a place of obligation, and so these hadiths contradict reason, he is ignorant. Obligation ends only upon entering the abode of permanence, Paradise or Hell. Otherwise, obligation exists in the intermediate realm (al-barzakh) and on the plains of resurrection (al-'arasat). That is why they will be called to prostrate before Him at the place of standing, and the believers will prostrate to Him willingly and by choice, while the disbelievers and hypocrites will be prevented from prostrating.

The point is this: no one at all has any excuse for disobeying Allah and opposing His command, while knowing this and being able to act or refrain. If he had an excuse, he would not deserve punishment or blame, neither in this world nor in the next.

If it is said: "This is speech in the tongue of the legal ruling (al-shar'), but if you spoke in the tongue of reality (al-haqiqah), you would excuse creation, since they are heading toward Allah's will concerning them and what He has decreed and ordained for them inevitably. They are subject to His decrees, and its arrows strike them, and they are targets for the arrows of the decrees, which never miss them at all. But whoever is dominated by witnessing the legal ruling cannot seek excuses for them, while whoever is dominated by witnessing the cosmic ruling (al-hukm al-kawni) excuses them. So you are excused in denouncing us by the reality of the law, and we are excused in seeking excuses by the reality of the ruling, and both of us are correct."

The answer is in several aspects:

First: It is said that if an excuse is not accepted, it is of no benefit, and excusing oneself by the decree is not accepted, and no one is excused by it. Even if one offers it, it is a false statement that accomplishes nothing at all. Rather, it increases the sin of the offender, and the Lord becomes angry with him. Something of this nature is not occupied with by an intelligent person.

Second: Excusing oneself by the decree implies absolving the offender himself and clearing his own position, though he is a wrongdoer and ignorant. Ascribing ignorance to the decree is ascribing sin to it, and doing injustice to it, both in tongue of state and tongue of speech, by beautifying and softening the expression. Often the state overcomes him, and he declares his grief openly, as one of the adversaries of Allah said:

"He threw him into the sea bound, and said to him: Beware, beware lest you get wet with water."

Another adversary said:

"They placed the meat for the falcons on the two peaks of Adan,
then blamed the falcons for slipping their tethers.
If they had wished to protect me, they would have covered your beautiful face."

Another adversary said:

"You have become affected by what you choose for me, so all my deeds are acts of obedience."

Another adversary, complaining and feeling wronged, said:

"If the lover has little fortune, then his good deeds are but sins."

Another adversary, making excuses for Iblis, said: "Since he disobeyed, whose Iblis was he?"

The adversaries of Allah have here complaints, grievances and reproaches. If they searched the corners of their hearts, they would find there an adversary who feels wronged, complaining, reproaching, saying: "I cannot say anything, and I am wronged in the form of a wrongdoer," and saying with anguish, sighing deeply: "Wretched is the son of Adam, neither able nor excused."

Another said: "The son of Adam is a ball beneath the mallets of the decrees: one strikes it, and another returns it. Can the ball ever avenge itself on the mallet?"

Another adversary quotes the poet's words:

"By my father, you are, even if you have been harsh in forsaking me and in wronging me,"

making Him one who forsakes without sin, a wrongdoer, indeed an extravagant one who has exceeded the limit in His injustice. Another says:

"A cloud once hung over us from You, one day, which shone lightning for us, but its sprinkling was slow.
So its cloud does not clear, that the seeker should despair, nor does its rain come, that its thirsty ones be quenched."

Another says:

"He draws near to you, but the lack of fortune keeps him away, and he goes straight while the calling of parting twists him."

Another adversary says:

"Standing in the water, thirsty, yet he is not given to drink."

Whoever has even a little understanding and insight knows that all this is injustice, complaint and reproach, and almost one of them would say: "O you who wronged me, if not for you!" If he searched his own self as he should, he would find this within it. There is no greater extent of ignorance and injustice than this. The human being, as Allah the Most High said: "Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant" (33:72), and "And Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy" (35:15).

If this wrongdoing, ignorant person knew that his affliction is from himself and his calamity from himself, and that he is more deserving of every blame and injustice, and that he is the home of every evil, and that "Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord" (100:6)—Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: this means disbelieving and denying the blessings of Allah.

Al-Hasan said: it is the one who counts calamities and forgets blessings.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is one of little good. And the land "kanud" is one in which nothing grows. It was also said: the one that produces none of the benefits. Al-Fadl ibn 'Abbas said: the kanud is one whom a single act of wrongdoing makes forget many acts of kindness.

If this wrongdoing, ignorant person knew that he is the one sitting on the road of his own interests, cutting them off from reaching him, that he is the stone in the path of the water on which his life depends, that he is the blockage that has stopped the flow of water to the garden of his heart, and yet cries out: "Thirst! Thirst!" while he himself stands in the path of the water and prevents its arrival to him, then he is the veil of his heart from the secret of its Unseen, the cloud that blocks the rising of the sun of guidance upon the heart. Nothing is more harmful to him than himself, and he has no enemies more able to harm and oppose him than himself.

"Enemies cannot reach from an ignorant man what the ignorant man reaches from himself."

Woe to him, a wrongdoer in the form of one wronged, a complainer while the offence is from himself. He has strived in turning away, while calling out: "They drove me away and distanced me!" He has turned his back on the door, rather he has locked it upon himself and lost its keys and broken them, and says:

"He called me, and closed the door before me. Is there a way to enter? Show me my case."

The compassionate one seizes him by his waistband away from the Fire, while he pulls against him, overcomes him, and plunges in, crying out: "What can I do? They brought me forward to the pit and threw me into it!" By Allah, how often the advisor has cried out to him: "Caution! Caution! Beware! Beware!" How often he has seized his garment, and how often he has shown him the corpses of those who plunged in, yet he refuses except to plunge in:

"How often have I poured advice upon your traces, though the advisor may gain suspicion."

Woe to him! A helper of Satan against his Lord, an adversary of Allah with his own self, compelled in sins, free-willed in acts of obedience, weak in judgment, squanderer of his opportunity, sitting idle from his own interests, reproaching the decrees of his Lord. He argues against his Lord with what he would not accept from his servant, his wife or his maidservant if they argued with it against him in neglecting some of his commands. If he commanded one of them to do something and they neglected it, or forbade them from something and they committed it, and said: "Fate drove me to that," he would not accept this argument from them, and would hasten to punish them.

If the decree is an argument for you, O wrongdoing ignorant one, in abandoning the right of your Lord, why would it not be an argument for your servant and maidservant in abandoning some of your right? Indeed, if a wrongdoer harms you, or a transgressor assaults you, and argues by the decree, your anger against him would increase, his offence would be multiplied in your eyes, you would see his argument as refuted, and then you argue with it against your Lord, and see it as an excuse for yourself! So who is more deserving of injustice and ignorance than one in such a state?

Moreover, Allah's kindness to you is continuous with every breath. He removed your ailments, enabled you to gather provision for His Paradise, sent you the guide, gave you the burden of the journey and what you need to provision yourself, and what you use to fight the highwaymen against you. He gave you hearing, sight and heart, made you know good and evil, beneficial and harmful, sent His messenger to you, sent down His book to you, made it easy for remembrance, understanding and action, and aided you with reinforcements from His noble army, who strengthen and guard you, fight your enemy and drive him away from you, and wish that you would not incline to him or make peace with him. They spare you his harm, yet you refuse except to support him against them and to befriend him instead of them. Rather, you support him and befriend him instead of your true protector, who is more deserving of you. Allah the Most High said: "And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated except Iblis; he was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are enemies to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers" (18:50).

He drove Iblis away from His heaven, expelled him from His Paradise, and distanced him from His nearness, because he did not prostrate to you while you were in the loins of your father Adam, out of your honour before Him. So he became hostile to him and distanced him. Then you befriended his enemy, inclined to him, and made peace with him, and yet you feel wronged, complaining of the expulsion and distancing, and saying:

"They taught me union, and union is sweet, then they threw me into severance, and severance is hard."

Yes, how could one not be driven away whose conduct is like this? How could one not be distanced whose state is this? How could He make among His intimates and people of nearness one whose state with Him is thus? He has corrupted and clouded what lies between him and Allah.

Allah commanded him to be grateful, not because He needs it, but so that he would gain more of His bounty. So making the denial of His blessings, and using them to disobey Him, one of the greatest causes of their removal from him.

He commanded him to remember Him, so that He would remind him of His kindness. So forgetting Him became a cause of Allah forgetting him: "They forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves" (59:19), and "They forgot Allah, so He forgot them" (9:67). He commanded him to ask Him, so that He would give to him. He did not ask, yet Allah gave him the greatest gifts without asking, and he did not accept. He complains to one who has mercy on him to one who has no mercy on him, feels wronged by one who does not wrong him, and abandons the one who opposes him and wrongs him. If Allah grants him health, well-being, wealth and position, he seeks help from these blessings for his acts of disobedience. If He takes these from him, he remains discontented with his Lord, and it is He whom he complains about. He is not fit for ease, nor for trial: ease casts him toward what displeases Allah, and trial drives him toward ingratitude, denial of His blessings, and complaint to His creation.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 33, verse 72 (part 2 of 2):**

He invited him to His door, but he did not stop at it or knock on it. Then He opened it for him, but he did not turn towards it or enter it. He sent His messenger to him, calling him to the abode of His honour, but he disobeyed the messenger and said: "I will not sell what is present for what is absent, or cash for credit, and I will not abandon what I see for something I have only heard of." And he says:

*"Take what you see and leave what you have only heard of,*
*for in the brightness of the sun there is what makes you need not Saturn."*

If what suits his fortune happens to be obeying the Messenger, he obeys him to gain his share, not for the pleasure of the One who sent him. He continues to earn God's hatred through his disobediences until He turns away from him and shuts the door in his face.

Despite all this, God does not make him despair of His mercy. Rather, He says: "Whenever you come to Me, I accept you. If you come to Me by night, I accept you; if you come to Me by day, I accept you. If you draw near to Me a span, I draw near to you a cubit; if you draw near to Me a cubit, I draw near to you a fathom; if you come to Me walking, I come to you running. If you meet Me with earth's fullness of sins, having not associated anything with Me, I will come to you with its fullness of forgiveness. Even if your sins reach the clouds of the sky, then you seek My forgiveness, I will forgive you. Who is greater than Me in generosity and bounty?

My servants defy Me with great sins, yet I watch over them on their beds. Indeed, I, the jinn and mankind are in a momentous matter: I create while others are worshipped, I provide while others are thanked. My good comes down to the servants, while their evil rises up to Me. I show them love through My blessings, though I am free of need of them, while they hate Me through their disobediences, though they are most in need of Me.

Whoever comes to Me, I meet him from afar; whoever turns away from Me, I call him from near; whoever leaves something for My sake, I give him more than he can imagine; whoever desires My pleasure, I desire what he desires; whoever acts by My power and strength, I soften iron for him.

The people of My remembrance are the people of My company; the people of My gratitude are the people of My increase; the people of My obedience are the people of My honour; and the people of My disobedience, I do not make them despair of My mercy. If they repent to Me, then I am their beloved, for I love those who repent and I love those who purify themselves. If they do not repent to Me, then I am their physician: I test them with calamities to purify them from their faults.

Whoever prefers Me over others, I prefer him over others. A good deed with Me is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times, and many more multiples. An evil deed with Me is counted as one. If he regrets it and seeks My forgiveness, I forgive it for him. I thank the little that is done, and I forgive the many slips. My mercy precedes My anger, My forbearance precedes My punishment, and My pardon precedes My retribution. I am more merciful to My servants than a mother to her child. God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than a man who lost his mount in a deadly, desolate land, on which were his food and drink. He searched for it until, despairing of finding it, he lay down under a tree to await death. Then he woke up and found it at his head, its halter caught in the tree. God is more joyful at the repentance of His servant than this man is at his mount."

This is the joy of benevolence, kindness and gentleness, not the joy of one in need who benefits from his servant's repentance. Likewise, His showing loyalty to His servant is out of benevolence, love and kindness towards him. It is not that He increases through him after being few, or is strengthened by him after being humbled, or gains victory through him after being defeated, or prepares him for a calamity, or seeks his help in a matter. Say, [as God says]: ﴿And say: "Praise be to God, who has not taken a son, and has no partner in the dominion, nor has He any protector out of weakness; so magnify Him with all magnificence."﴾ [al-Isra' 17:111]. He negated that He has any protector out of weakness, and God is the Protector of those who believe, and they are His friends.

This is the matter of the Lord and the matter of the servant. Yet the servants make excuses for their own selves and attribute their sins to His decree.

*"God has monopolised praise and glory,*
*and has turned blame away from the man."*

How beautifully the poet said:

*"You travel tirelessly away from your beloved,*
*while you remain weeping for him with flowing tears.*
*Your own soul has deceived you: you are not of his beloved ones;*
*you complain of separation, while you are the one who wrongs."*

This is one of the two meanings of his saying: "Among the realities of repentance is seeking excuses for creation."

It has become clear to you from this that seeking excuses for their wrongdoing returns to repentance by nullifying and invalidating it.

[Section: Among the Realities of Repentance Is Seeking Excuses for Creation]

The second meaning: that he intends to establish excuses for their wrongs against you, and their offences against you, and to look at this in terms of the decree, that their actions are like the movements of trees. So you excuse them by the decree regarding your right, not regarding the right of your Lord. This is true, and it is one of the traits of the masters of the knowers and the elite of God's perfected saints. Such a person annihilates himself regarding his own right and fulfils the right of his Lord. He looks at negligence regarding his own right, and at offences against himself, in terms of the decree; and he looks at God's right in terms of the command. So he seeks excuses for them regarding his own right, and he refuses to excuse them and holds them accountable regarding God's right.

This was the state of our Prophet ﷺ, as 'Ā'ishah (may God be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ never took revenge for himself at all, nor was anything done to him that he took revenge for himself for, unless the sanctities of God were violated. When the sanctities of God were violated, nothing could stand against his anger until he took revenge for God."

'Ā'ishah (may God be pleased with her) also said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ never struck a servant with his hand, nor an animal, nor anything at all, unless it was in the path of God."

Anas (may God be pleased with him) said: "I served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years, and he never said to me about something I had done: 'Why did you do it?' nor about something I had not done: 'Why did you not do it?' And if some of his family rebuked me, he would say: 'Leave him, for if something was decreed, it would have happened.'"

So look at his view of the decree in regard to his own right, and his standing firm in the command, and how he cut off the woman's hand in regard to God's right, without saying there: "The decree judged against her."

Likewise, his intention to burn those who stayed away from congregational prayer with him, and he did not say: "If prayer had been decreed for them, they would have prayed."

Likewise, his stoning of the woman and the man when they committed adultery, and he did not argue for them by the decree.

Likewise, his action regarding the 'Uraniyyin, who killed his shepherd, drove off the camels, and disbelieved after their Islam. He did not say: "It was decreed for them." Rather, he ordered that their hands and feet be cut off on opposite sides, their eyes be branded with hot iron, and they be left in al-Harrah to beg for water, yet they were not given water until they died of thirst, along with other things too lengthy to detail.

The Messenger of God ﷺ was too knowing of God and of His right to argue by the decree for abandoning His command, or to accept such an argument from anyone. Yet with all this, he excused Anas by the decree regarding his own right, and said: "If something was decreed, it would have happened." May the blessings and peace of God be upon him.

This second meaning, though true, is not among the conditions of repentance, nor among its pillars, nor is it connected to it. For if one did not establish excuses for those who wronged him, that would not diminish his repentance in any way. He only intended the first meaning, and you have known what is wrong with it.

There is no doubt that the author of *al-Manazil* only intended to excuse them by the decree and to establish the judgement of the command over them, so that he looks through the eye of the decree and excuses them by it, and looks through the eye of the command and holds them to its requirements. Thus the contemplation of the command does not veil him from the decree, nor the attention to the decree veil him from the command.

This, though a truth that cannot be dispensed with, offers no justification for excusing them. Their excuse has nothing to do with repentance at all. Even if it were valid, let alone if it were false, they would not be excused, and seeking their excuse is not among the realities of repentance. Rather, the truth is that zeal for God and anger for Him are among the realities of repentance. To nullify the excuse of creation regarding opposition to the command and prohibition, and to be extremely angry, is one of the signs of honouring the sacred prohibitions. It is part of the realities of repentance that one prioritises this over the excuse for disobeying the command and prohibition.

Especially since this includes the excuse of the idol and image worshippers, the murderers of the prophets, Pharaoh and Haman, Nimrod son of Canaan, Abu Jahl and his companions, Iblis and his armies, and every disbeliever and wrongdoer who transgresses God's limits and violates His sanctities. All of them are under the decree and are part of creation. Would the excuse of these people be part of the reality of repentance?

This is what the journey along the path of annihilation in the Oneness of Lordship necessitates, and it is the goal to which the travellers aspire.

Moreover, what agreement with the Beloved is there in excusing one whom He Himself does not excuse? Indeed, His anger against him has intensified, He has distanced him from His nearness, expelled him from His door, and hated him with the utmost hatred. So if you excuse him, will his excuse be anything other than an exposure to the Beloved's wrath and a fall from His sight?

This slip does not, however, require us to nullify the virtues of Shaykh al-Islam or to think ill of him. His position in knowledge, leadership, gnosis, and precedence on the path of spiritual wayfaring is a station that cannot be ignored. Everyone's words are taken and rejected except those of the Infallible, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him. The perfect one is one whose error is counted, especially in such a narrow field and difficult battleground, where feet have slipped, understandings have gone astray, and the paths of the travellers have diverged, and most of them, except a few, have come to the edge of the valleys of destruction.

And how could it not be so? It is the sea in which the ship of its rider sails through waves like mountains, the battlefield before whose sight the courage of heroes shrinks, and in which the intellects of the wisest men are bewildered. And creation has reached its shore, desiring to ride it.

Among them is one who stands still, astonished, unable to fill his eye with it, nor to move his foot from his position, his heart full with the greatness of what he has witnessed. He says: "Standing on the shore is safer, and he who risks himself is not wise."

Among them is one who turns back on his heels when he hears its roar and the sound of its waves, and cannot bear to look at it.

Among them is one who throws himself into its depths, pushed down by one wave and lifted up by another.

These three are in danger: the one standing on the shore is exposed to the water reaching his feet; the one who flees, even if he strives hard in fleeing, has no destination but to it; and the one who ventures sees the drowned every moment with his own eyes. Only the fourth category has been saved from among creation: those who waited for the arrival of the ship of command. When it drew near to them, its captain called out to them: ﴿Embark therein; in the name of God is its course and its mooring﴾ [Hud 11:41]. This is truly the ship of Noah, and the ship of the messengers after him. Whoever boarded it was saved, and whoever stayed behind it drowned. They boarded the ship of command by the decree, sailing with them through the shifting of its waves, under the rule of submission to the One who holds the control of the seas. And it was but a moment's slumber until it was said to the earth and the sky of this world: "O earth, swallow your water; O sky, withhold!" The water subsided, the matter was decided, and the ship came to rest on al-Judi, the abode of permanence.

Those who stayed behind the ship, like the people of Noah, were drowned, then burned. They were called out upon before all the worlds: ﴿And it was said: "Away with the wrongdoing people!"﴾ [Hud 11:44]. ﴿We did not wrong them, but they were the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Zukhruf 43:76]. Then it was proclaimed in the tongue of the Law and of the decree, confirming His oneness and establishing His proof, and He is the most just of judges: ﴿Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof; had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ [al-An'am 6:149].
